body:
## Summary
This PR adds a new hydration goal configuration step to the onboarding wizard and updates the hydration tracker to use personalized settings instead of hardcoded values. Users can now set their daily water intake goal based on body weight and activity level, with the ability to customize cup size.

## Key Changes

- **New Wizard Slide (Step 9)**: Added "Your Hydration Goal" slide that:
  - Calculates recommended daily water intake using formula: weight (kg) × 33ml + activity level bonus
  - Allows users to adjust the goal with +/- buttons (250ml increments)
  - Provides cup/bottle size selection (200ml, 250ml, 350ml, 500ml)
  - Displays calculated number of cups needed per day
  - Saves settings to localStorage and sessionStorage for persistence

- **Water Goal Calculation Logic**: Implemented `calculateWaterGoal()` function that:
  - Uses standard hydration guideline (33ml per kg body weight)
  - Applies activity level adjustments (sedentary: 0ml, light: +250ml, moderate: +500ml, very: +750ml)
  - Rounds to nearest 50ml for cleaner numbers

- **Hydration Tracker Updates**: Modified tracker to use personalized settings:
  - Replaced hardcoded 8 glasses/2000ml with dynamic values from localStorage
  - Updated display to show "X / Goal ml" format
  - Updated hint text to show actual glass size (e.g., "Tap to add 250ml")
  - Added goal display in hydration section header
  - Circle color changes to green when goal is reached

- **Onboarding Flow**: Incremented total wizard steps from 20 to 21 and renumbered all subsequent slides (10-20 → 11-21)

- **Data Persistence**: Water goal settings sync from database to localStorage on app load for cross-device consistency

## Implementation Details

- Settings stored in localStorage as: `pbb_water_goal_ml`, `pbb_water_glass_size`, `pbb_water_total_glasses`
- Also saved to sessionStorage userProfile for database synchronization
- Wizard slide includes visual feedback with gradient backgrounds and interactive buttons
- Glass count updates dynamically as user adjusts goal or cup size

## Summary

- Add WebAssembly plugin support for custom rule logic via sandboxed Wasmtime runtime
- Users can write rule conditions in any language that compiles to WASM (Rust, Go, AssemblyScript, etc.)
- New `acteon-wasm-runtime` crate with fuel-based CPU limits, memory caps, and no WASI/host imports
- Full-stack: rule engine integration (YAML + CEL), server API, admin UI, all 5 SDKs, 68 tests, 15-scenario simulation

## Changes

**Core runtime** (`crates/wasm-runtime/`):
- `WasmPluginRuntime` trait + Wasmtime v29 implementation
- Plugin registry with fuel-based CPU limits (default 100ms), memory limiter (default 16MB)
- `SharedWasmRegistry` async wrapper, `MockWasmRuntime`/`FailingWasmRuntime` for tests
- Plugin ABI: `evaluate(input_ptr, input_len) -> i32` with JSON I/O

**Rule engine**:
- `Expr::WasmCall` condition variant + `RuleSource::Wasm`
- YAML: `wasm_plugin`/`wasm_function` condition keys
- CEL: `wasm("plugin", "function")` built-in function
- Full trace integration for Rule Playground

**Server**:
- `[wasm]` config section with `plugin_dir` and default resource limits
- `GET/DELETE /v1/plugins` API with `Permission::PluginsManage` auth
- Prometheus metrics: `wasm_invocations`, `wasm_errors`

**UI**:
- WASM Plugins management page (list, register, delete, test invocation panel)
- Rule Playground updated to show WASM trace details

**SDKs**: All 5 updated (Rust, Python, Node.js, Go, Java) with types, methods, and tests

**Security** (reviewed by dedicated security agent):
- RwLock contention fix (clone Module under lock, release before WASM execution)
- `PluginsManage` permission on delete endpoint
- Config validation at runtime level
- Wasmtime v29 API compatibility fixes

**Quality**:
- 68 new unit tests across 10 files
- 15-scenario simulation with 7 mock runtimes
- Feature + architecture documentation

author: artilleryjoe
body:
### Motivation
- Provide advanced, cyber threat-aware RAG capabilities so the Cybersandbox can ingest, tag, and retrieve intelligence with analyst-friendly filtering and scoring for modern threats.
- Enable modular ingestion and retrieval modes to support semantic, hybrid, and threat-intel–focused workflows for pragmatic security briefings.

### Description
- Implemented a new threat-aware RAG backend in `iron_dillo_cybersandbox_ai/backend/rag.py` including threat-family regexes, MITRE-style tactic detection, CVE/technique indicator extraction, chunk metadata enrichment, and selectable chunking (`fixed` or `paragraph`).
- Added hybrid rescoring that combines semantic similarity, keyword overlap, and threat-tag alignment with scoped query filters via `doc_ids` and `required_threat_tags`, and exposed retrieval modes `vector`, `hybrid`, and `intel` via `query_rag` arguments.
- Extended FastAPI contracts in `iron_dillo_cybersandbox_ai/backend/main.py` to accept `retrieval_mode`, `doc_ids`, and `required_threat_tags` on `POST /rag/query` and a `chunk_mode` query parameter for `POST /rag/ingest` and added input validation and audit logging for these options.
- Reworked Cybersandbox settings loader to avoid `BaseSettings` compatibility issues in this runtime by using a lightweight `Settings` model and environment-driven `get_settings()` that reads expected env vars.
- Documented the new capabilities in `iron_dillo_cybersandbox_ai/README.md` under an "Advanced modular RAG" section and added unit tests `tests/test_cybersandbox_rag.py` covering ingestion metadata, hybrid filtering/scoring, and invalid retrieval mode handling.

### Testing
- Ran targeted tests with `pytest -q tests/test_cybersandbox_rag.py tests/test_tools.py` which passed successfully.
- Ran the full test suite with `pytest -q` and observed all tests passing (`17 passed`) in this environment.

author: viandoxdev
body:
This PR addresses significant performance issues across the app:

1.  **Review Screen Freeze**: The `ReviewScreen` was compiling all cards on the main thread, causing the app to freeze when opening a large study. This has been moved to a background thread with a proper loading state.
2.  **Search Jank**: The `ExploreViewModel` was re-mapping and re-emitting search results every 50ms even if nothing changed. This is now optimized to check for changes first.
3.  **Statistics Lag**: The `StatisticsViewModel` was calculating stats on the main thread. This is now offloaded to `Dispatchers.Default`.

author: copilot
body:
Implements missing infrastructure for `workflow_runner.py`'s 7-phase pipeline (plan→design→build→test→doc→package→release). Enables issue-triggered agent dispatch and nightly health monitoring.

## Prompt Library

Created/enhanced 7 phase prompts in `.github/workflow/prompts/`:
- All prompts now reference AGENTS.md critical rules (PrivilegedCommand unpacking, no `sudo`, timeout enforcement, etc.)
- Renamed `implement.md` → `build.md` for consistency with workflow_runner.py
- Total: 13.3KB of structured prompts with exit criteria and validation steps

```markdown
# Example: build.md excerpt
CRITICAL RULES (from AGENTS.md):
- Always unpack PrivilegedCommand: binary, args, desc = PrivilegedCommand.dnf(...)
- Never hardcode dnf — use SystemManager.get_package_manager()
- Always timeout=N on subprocess calls
- Never subprocess in UI — extract to utils/, use CommandRunner
```

## GitHub Actions Workflows

### agent-dispatch.yml (8.5KB)
- Triggers: `agent-task` label on issues OR manual workflow_dispatch
- Extracts version from issue title/body via regex `v?(\d+\.\d+\.?\d*)`
- **Defaults to `--dry-run`** (requires explicit `live_run: true` to modify repo)
- Posts execution output as issue comment
- Supports all 7 phases × 3 assistants (copilot, claude, codex)

### nightly-agents.yml (5.8KB)
- Schedule: Daily at 03:00 UTC
- Validates AgentRegistry (`utils/agents.py`), runs lint/typecheck/smoke tests
- Uploads health report artifact
- Fails if any check fails

## Shell Wrapper

Enhanced `scripts/workflow-runner.sh` with dual-mode interface:
- **Modern**: `--phase X --target-version Y --assistant Z`
- **Legacy**: `<version> <phase> [args...]` (backward compatible, maps `implement→build`, `document→doc`)
- Validates Python 3.12+, auto-sets PYTHONPATH

## Directory Structure

Created `.workflow/issue-tracker/.gitkeep` (referenced by workflow_runner.py's `artifact_paths()` function)

## Model Router

Verified existing `model-router.toml` matches `DEFAULT_PHASE_MODELS`:
- Brain tier (gpt-5.3-codex): plan, design
- Labor tier (gpt-4o): build, test
- Labor-light tier (gpt-4o-mini): doc, package, release

## Usage

```bash
# Issue-based (automatic): Label issue with "agent-task", version in title → dry-run dispatch
# Manual dispatch: Actions → Agent Dispatch → set live_run: true for live execution
# Shell: ./scripts/workflow-runner.sh --phase plan --target-version v42.0.0 --assistant copilot --dry-run
```

## Files Changed

**Modified** (9): All 7 prompts, `workflow_runner.py` (build.md ref), `workflow-runner.sh` (rewrite)  
**Created** (3): `agent-dispatch.yml`, `nightly-agents.yml`, `.workflow/issue-tracker/.gitkeep`

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Overview

Set up the best automated AI agent workflow for the repository. The repo already has a mature `scripts/workflow_runner.py` that implements a 7-phase pipeline (plan → design → build → test → doc → package → release) supporting Copilot, Claude, and Codex backends — but it's missing critical infrastructure files that it references. Additionally, we need new GitHub Actions workflows to automate agent dispatch from issues.

## What Needs to Be Created

### 1. Prompt Library (`.github/workflow/prompts/`)

The `workflow_runner.py` references `PROMPTS_DIR = ROOT / ".github" / "workflow" / "prompts"` (line 35) but the directory doesn't exist. Create these 7 prompt files that the runner's `run_phase()` function expects:

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/plan.md`** — P1 PLAN phase prompt. Instructions for the AI agent to read `ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and agent memory, then produce a task specification file (`.workflow/specs/tasks-vX.Y.Z.md`) with tasks in the required format: `ID:`, `Files:`, `Dep:`, `Agent:`, `Description:`, `Acceptance:`, `Docs:`, `Tests:`.

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/design.md`** — P2 DESIGN phase prompt. Instructions to read the tasks spec and produce an architecture document (`.workflow/specs/arch-vX.Y.Z.md`) and a release notes draft (`.workflow/specs/release-notes-draft-vX.Y.Z.md`).

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/build.md`** — P3 BUILD phase prompt. Instructions to implement all tasks from the task spec, following the project's code patterns: `utils/` for business logic (`@staticmethod`, operations tuples), `ui/` for PyQt6 tabs (inherit `BaseTab`), `cli/` for CLI commands. Must follow all critical rules from `AGENTS.md` (never sudo, never hardcode dnf, always timeout, etc.).

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/test.md`** — P4 TEST phase prompt. Instructions to write tests for all new code using `unittest` + `unittest.mock`, `@patch` decorators only, mock all system calls, test success AND failure paths, output a test report JSON.

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/document.md`** — P5 DOC phase prompt. Instructions to update `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep-a-Changelog format), `README.md`, and finalize release notes from the draft.

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/package.md`** — P6 PACKAGE phase prompt. Instructions to validate version alignment across `version.py`, `.spec`, and `pyproject.toml`, and ensure packaging scripts are correct.

- **`.github/workflow/prompts/release.md`** — P7 RELEASE phase prompt. Instructions to prepare the final release manifest using only provided artifacts, without executing shell commands.

Each prompt should reference the project's conventions from `AGENTS.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

### 2. Model Router (`.github/workflow/model-router.toml`)

The `workflow_runner.py` references `MODEL_ROUTER_FILE = ROOT / ".github" / "workflow" / "model-router.toml"` (line 34). Create this TOML config file with model assignments per phase matching the defaults in `workflow_runner.py`:

```toml
[models]
plan = "gpt-5.3-codex"
design = "gpt-5.3-codex"
build = "gpt-4o"
test = "gpt-4o"
doc = "gpt-4o-mini"
package = "gpt-4o-mini"
release = "gpt-4o-mini"
```

### 3. Agent Dispatch Workflow (`.github/workflows/agent-dispatch.yml`)

Create a new GitHub Actions workflow that:
- Triggers on issues labeled `agent-task`
- Extracts the target version from the issue title/body (pattern: `vX.Y.Z`)
- Runs `scripts/workflow_runner.py --phase all --target-version <version> --assistant copilot --mode write --issue <issue_number> --dry-run` (dry-run by default for safety)
- Posts a comment on the issue with the execution plan/results
- Can be overridden to run without `--dry-run` via workflow_dispatch with a `live_run` boolean input

### 4. Nightly Agent Health Check (`.github/workflows/nightly-agents.yml`)

Create a scheduled workflow that:
- Runs daily at 03:00 UTC
- Also supports `workflow_dispatch`
- Runs the project's built-in system agents in dry-run/check mode by executing:
  ```bash
  PYTHONPATH=loofi-fedora-tweaks python -c "
  from utils.agents import AgentRegistry
  registry = AgentRegistry.instance()
  summary = registry.get_agent_summary()
  print(f'Total: {summary[\"total_agents\"]}')
  print(f'Enabled: {summary[\"enabled\"]}')
  "
  ```
- Runs a quick lint + typecheck + test smoke to verify repo health
- Creates a summary as a workflow artifact

### 5. Workflow Runner Shell Wrapper (`scripts/workflow-runner.sh`)

Create a convenience shell script that:
- Sets up PYTHONPATH
- Validates Python 3.12+ is available
- Forwards all arguments to `python scripts/workflow_runner.py`
- Provides usage help when called with `--help` or no arguments
- Make it executable

### 6. Ensure `.workflow/` directories exist

Create placeholder `.gitkeep` files in:
- `.workflow/specs/.gitkeep`
- `.workflow/reports/.gitkeep`
- `.workflow/issue-tracker/.gitkeep`

These directories are referenced by `workflow_runner.py`'s `artifact_paths()` function but may not all exist.

body:
I have fixed the issue where the bot failed to respond to your Discord message and implemented several performance optimizations.

**Key Changes:**
1. **Discord Fix**: Added a retry mechanism for simple DMs (like "How are you?"). Previously, if these generated "AI slop," the bot would simply stay silent. Now, it will retry up to 3 times, giving itself feedback to avoid the specific slop it just generated.
2. **Vision Optimization**: 
   - **Parallel Processing**: The bot now analyzes all images in your recent chat history simultaneously rather than one-by-one, which was a major source of delay.
   - **Caching**: Analysis results are now cached for 1 hour. If you keep talking in a thread with an image, the bot won't re-analyze that image every single time you speak.
3. **Transparency**: Discord logs now explicitly state which forbidden phrase (e.g., "digital heartbeat") triggered a slop filter, rather than a generic error message.

**30 Proposals to Speed Up Discord Responses:**

1. **Parallelize Vision Analysis**: (Implemented) Process all historical images simultaneously.
2. **Vision Result Caching**: (Implemented) Cache image descriptions by URL to avoid redundant API calls.
3. **Fast-Path for Simple Admin DMs**: Use a faster model (e.g., Step-3.5-Flash) for non-philosophical greetings.
4. **Parallel Planning & Drafting**: Trigger pre-planning intuition and initial draft generation at the same time.
5. **Streaming Responses**: Chunks can be sent to Discord as they generate to reduce perceived latency.
6. **Context Trimming**: Reduce the history window for planning from 20 messages to 10-12.
7. **System Prompt Compression**: Remove redundant instructions or move static configs to background tasks.
8. **Independent Tool Parallelization**: Execute Search, Wikipedia, and Profile Analysis in parallel.
9. **Early Safety Exit**: Terminate processing immediately if a safety violation is detected.
10. **Social Context Caching**: Cache the "Daily Narrative" from Bluesky for 10 minutes instead of re-fetching per turn.
11. **Vector Memory Retrieval**: Use semantic search instead of formatting the whole memory thread into the prompt.
12. **Background Context Updating**: Save fact extraction and channel summaries *after* replying to the user.
13. **Selective Vision**: Only re-analyze history images if they are specifically referenced.
14. **Adaptive Retry Limits**: Lower retry counts during high-arousal or high-traffic periods.
15. **Pre-fetched Social History**: Periodically sync social data in the background.
16. **Persistent API Connections**: Use HTTP Keep-Alive to reduce TLS handshake overhead with providers.
17. **Skip Variety Checks for DMs**: Disable expensive LLM-based repetition checks for private admin chat.
18. **Model Tiering**: Use Qwen 480B only for final synthesis; use smaller models for brainstorming.
19. **Prompt Pruning**: Dynamically remove irrelevant tool definitions based on conversation keywords.
20. **Optimized Local Slop Check**: Use highly optimized local regex for known clichés before calling an LLM.
21. **History Fetch Throttling**: Only refresh Discord history if the local cache is older than 5 minutes.
22. **Parallel Link Summarization**: Summarize multiple web links concurrently.
23. **Reduced Temperature for Planning**: Use lower temperature for deterministic (and often faster) planning logic.
24. **Administrative Auto-Approve**: Skip the "Reflector" loop turn for common admin-requested actions.
25. **Jitter Delay Reduction**: Dynamically shorten artificial "typing" delays when in "high energy" mode.
26. **Selective Tool Injecting**: Only pass tool schemas to the LLM that match the current interaction context.
27. **Hard Length Caps**: Enforce strict token limits on simple response types.
28. **Vision Model Switching**: Use a lightweight vision model (e.g., Moondream) for non-critical descriptions.
29. **Intuition Caching**: Reuse previous pre-planning intuition if the topic hasn't changed.
30. **Regional Endpoint Optimization**: Ensure API calls are routed to the geographically nearest NIM endpoint.

author: copilot
body:
When server reports essence gain via `UNIT_POWER_UPDATE`, timer must reset to resync with authoritative state. Previous logic used double negative (`not essenceSpent`) which obscured intent and risked breaking during refactoring.

## Changes

**Added explicit gain detection:**
```lua
local essenceGained = essenceChanged and currentEssence > self.lastEssenceCount
```

**Restructured timer reset with clear priority:**
```lua
// Before: implicit via double negative
if not essenceSpent or wasAtMax then
    self.lastEssenceTime = GetTime()
end

// After: explicit server resync
if essenceGained or wasAtMax or not essenceChanged then
    self.lastEssenceTime = GetTime()
elseif essenceSpent then
    // Carryover progress from partial state
end
```

**Behavior unchanged:**
- Essence gained (API) → reset timer
- Spell from max → reset timer  
- Spell from partial → keep timer (carryover)
- First init → reset timer

Protects against client prediction errors when server completes essence earlier than local timer predicts.

- Covers scenario-based testing (YAML-driven), convergence assertions, fault injection, and failure diagnostics

- Go + client-go + kind as the tech stack

body:
## Summary

Fixes test failures introduced by Renovate PR #187 (lock file maintenance) which bumps FastMCP from 2.12.4 to 2.14.5 and mcp from 1.14.1 to 1.26.0.

## Root Causes

1. **FastMCP 2.14.5** changed `without_injected_parameters` to strip `Context` params from resource `.fn()` wrappers, making them accept zero positional arguments
2. **MCP Client initialization** now consumes 3 rate-limited requests (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list) instead of 2
3. **Matrix edge case tests** exhaust the global 100/min rate limit when run after the full suite

## Changes (test-only, no production code)

- **test_persistence.py**: Use `set_context()` context manager instead of passing `mock_context` to `get_workspace.fn()`
- **test_math_operations.py**: Adjust rate limit loop from `range(8)` to `range(7)` to account for 3 init requests
- **test_matrix_operations.py**: Switch 2 edge case tests to `http_client_high_limit` fixture
- **conftest.py**: Add `reset_rate_limit` autouse fixture and `http_server_high_limit`/`http_client_high_limit` fixtures for test isolation

## Testing

All 159 tests pass locally. Lint clean. No production code changes.

body:
This pull request introduces several major improvements to the backend, focusing on authentication, observability, and developer experience. The most significant changes include the implementation of a full authentication system (with signup, login, password hashing, and JWT support), the integration of Prometheus metrics for observability, and the addition of Swagger API documentation. There are also upgrades to dependencies, Prisma configuration improvements, and enhanced error handling.

**Authentication System Implementation:**

- Added a comprehensive authentication module with signup and login endpoints, password hashing using `argon2`, and JWT-based authentication. This includes `AuthController`, `AuthService`, local strategy, and integration with the `UsersService` and Prisma. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-37d3279a8a78f12b16e161930290bf0ef16b705cb8d225e1382f364702ecaaf9L1-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aea62a4c305374791411369a46e8553d716a032a03bb48136176873887e3311cL1-R57) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d5cfad084289d1504e5322be173d5f5af9b85f4f90316b440e269218e18bc457L2-R23) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-9f241e772171d8de20cca901fff682bd66bf26973c7dee541621654050bd8018L8-R8)
- Introduced DTOs with validation and Swagger decorators for user creation and login.

**Observability and Metrics:**

- Integrated Prometheus metrics collection using `@willsoto/nestjs-prometheus` and a custom middleware that tracks request counts, durations, and errors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7b1cf858eddb148d3fa7f1c37e96476d5cf0ec7dd3d9444263f3f18fa408fe4fR1-R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-089f4f2474b64391c42b6e66aed33977e132058d92108f0a63234a7862e1f8b8L10-R39)
- Registered the middleware globally in `AppModule` to monitor all routes.

**API Documentation:**

- Added Swagger/OpenAPI documentation generation and setup, including endpoint grouping and JWT bearer authentication support.
- Enhanced DTOs with `@ApiProperty` for better documentation. (Fe0b0b7cL1)

**Prisma and Database Improvements:**

- Refactored `PrismaService` to improve configuration, add logging, support for connection pooling, and provide accessors for all models. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d1f18750dbbcd83f8fd7d8ec370e8557c51a17d9dcc9d7dc8a1e39d76c0f3c8aL1-R74) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f8c7567d5c98cdee7ef45de6a8e81f38596ece4fc6124b56c0ccd34e184adc86L6-R7)
- Updated Prisma and related dependencies to the latest versions and adjusted config paths to match the new project structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L29-R55) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L58-R67) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c96950ab4b66f64a7a92db38b944cc2f9ba2b5a122969252d565586ed4e73e55L7-R9)

**Error Handling and Miscellaneous:**

- Added a global HTTP exception filter for standardized error responses.
- Various dependency updates and minor improvements, such as fallback secrets for JWT and correct cookie parser usage. author: alexyboyer
body:
## Summary

Builds on the EU/UK/FR/DE locale work (#35) to add interactive locale selection during initialization and config management.

- **Interactive locale selection during `dam init`**: After KEK setup, users pick which regional PII patterns to enable via a `dialoguer::MultiSelect` checkbox prompt. Global patterns are always active and shown as a static label. OS locale auto-detection (via `sys-locale`) pre-selects likely regions (e.g. `en-US` → US, `fr-CA` → CA+FR, `de-*` → DE+EU). Non-TTY environments fall back to OS-detected locales without prompting.
- **`dam config get KEY`**: New subcommand to read config values (`detection.locales`, `detection.sensitivity`, `server.http_port`).
- **`dam config set detection.locales`**: Parses comma-separated locale input (e.g. `us,ca`) or `all` shorthand. Always includes Global, deduplicates.
- **Removed dead locale variants**: JP, KR, IN, CN had no patterns, no locale docs, and no implementation — removed from enum, `all()`, `FromStr`, `Display`, and the `build_patterns()` match arm.
- **Updated docs**: `docs/locales/README.md` table updated (EU/UK/FR/DE now linked), `README.md` quickstart mentions locale selection, config example shows `locales` field, CLI reference includes `dam config get`.

> **Note**: This PR depends on #35 (EU/UK/FR/DE locales). Merge #35 first.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — 452 tests pass (16 new tests for OS locale detection, locale list parsing)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` — zero warnings
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [ ] Manual: `dam init` shows interactive checkbox, selected locales written to config
- [ ] Manual: `dam config set detection.locales us,fr` then `dam config get detection.locales` shows `global, us, fr`
- [ ] Manual: `dam config set detection.locales all` shows all 7 locales in config
- [ ] Manual: pipe stdin (`echo | dam init`) uses non-interactive fallback

Closes #18

author: cs121
body:
### Motivation

- Vereinheitlichung der verstreuten Fog-Steuerung in einem einzigen, klaren CVAR-Namespace und einer einzigen Render-API, um doppelte Implementierungen und inkonsistente Defaults zu vermeiden. 
- Schaffung deterministischer Feature-Gates, damit Froxel- und Fogvol-Pfade nicht parallel laufen und sich gegenseitig unerwartet beeinflussen. 
- Aufbau einer auditierbaren Basis (Messbarkeit/Debug/Validate) bevor tiefere Qualitäts- und Bugfix-Phasen erfolgen.

### Description

- Neues zentrales CVAR-Set `r_fog_*` eingeführt und registriert, darunter `r_fog_enable`, `r_fog_backend`, `r_fog_density`, `r_fog_quality`, `r_fog_temporal`, `r_fog_history_weight`, `r_fog_jitter`, `r_fog_anisotropy`, `r_fog_debug` und `r_fog_validate`, deklariert in `Quake/gl_rmain.c` und registriert in `Quake/gl_rmisc.c`. 
- Zentrale Settings-Leser `Atmosphere_ReadSettings` erweitert und Backend-Auswahl vereinheitlicht (Backend: `0=legacy`, `1=froxel`, `2=fogvol-fallback`) sowie physikalische Parameter (z.B. `anisotropy`) an die neuen CVARs gebunden in `Quake/gl_rmain.c`. 
- Fog-Lifecycle-API eingeführt und genutzt: `R_Fog_BeginFrame`, `R_Fog_Render`, `R_Fog_Composite`, `R_Fog_EndFrame`, wobei `R_Atmosphere_Render` nun diese klaren Schritte aufruft (gleiche Steuerung von Froxel vs Fogvol). 
- FogVol wurde an die zentrale Steuerung angebunden durch `R_FogVol_ReadSettings` und die Laufzeitpfade angepasst, inklusive Temporal/History/Validate/Hazard-Gating und einmaligen Deprecation-Warnungen in `Quake/r_fogvol.c`. 
- Kleine Shader/dispatch- und uniform-Änderungen und Gating: Froxel temporal resolve respektiert `r_fog_temporal`, Froxel anisotropy-Uniforms verwenden den neuen `r_fog_anisotropy`, und Froxel jitter wird über `r_fog_jitter` gesteuert (Änderungen in `Quake/gl_rmain.c`). 
- Dokumentation erstellt: `docs/fog_audit.md` (Pipeline, FBOs, Shader-Inventar, Truth Table) und `docs/fog_cvars.md` (neuer Namespace + Migrationstabelle Alt→Neu). 

### Testing

- `git diff --check` wurde lokal ausgeführt und gab keine style-/whitespace-Fehler aus. 
- Versuchter CMake-Konfigurations- und Buildlauf (`cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build`) wurde automatisiert ausgeführt, die Konfiguration schlug fehl wegen fehlender System-Abhängigkeit (`SDL2Config.cmake` nicht gefunden), daher wurde kein vollständiger Build-Test abgeschlossen.

------

💡 **What:** Replaced `os.listdir()` with `os.scandir()` in `scripts/sync_zenn.py`, `scripts/sync_devto.py`, and `scripts/prepare_velog.py`.

🎯 **Why:** `os.scandir()` yields `DirEntry` objects that contain file attribute information (like `is_file()`), avoiding additional system calls compared to `os.listdir()` followed by `os.path` checks. It also avoids `os.path.join()` by using `entry.path`.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** In a benchmark with 5000 markdown files and 500 directories, the optimized `os.scandir` approach showed a **~50% reduction in time** for the directory traversal loop (from ~0.010s to ~0.005s per iteration). While total execution time is dominated by file I/O, this change improves efficiency and robustness.

### Motivation

- Corrigir incompatibilidade do JSON do bioma que usava chave `attributes` e cores em `#hex` (formato diferente do restante do projeto), o que pode levar ao bioma ser rejeitado pelo codec em tempo de execução. 
- Tornar a inserção do bioma no Overworld realizável ao substituir um ponto climático exato por faixas (`ranges`) para que a seleção multi-noise do Overworld tenha probabilidade prática de gerar o bioma.

### Description

- Atualizei `src/main/resources/data/dreamsdimensions/worldgen/biome/lumina_hollows.json` para usar o formato padrão de biomas do projeto, movendo valores de visual para `effects` com cores numéricas (`sky_color`, `water_color`, `water_fog_color`, `fog_color`, `foliage_color`, `grass_color`) e adicionando os blocos `spawners` e `spawn_costs` esperados pelo codec. 
- Atualizei `src/main/resources/data/dreamsdimensions/worldgen/biome_modifier/lumina_hollows_overworld_spawn.json` para converter `climate_parameter` de valores escalares para `range arrays` concretos (por exemplo, `"temperature": [0.55, 0.80]`, `"weirdness": [-0.25, 0.90]`, etc.), ampliando a janela climática em que o bioma pode aparecer. 
- Mantive `src/main/resources/data/dreamsdimensions/worldgen/biome_modifier/lumina_hollows_flora.json` inalterado porque é apenas um `neoforge:add_features` e não influencia a seleção do bioma pelo `/locate`.

### Testing

- Executado `jq . src/main/resources/data/dreamsdimensions/worldgen/biome/lumina_hollows.json` e `jq . src/main/resources/data/dreamsdimensions/worldgen/biome_modifier/lumina_hollows_overworld_spawn.json` para validação de sintaxe JSON — resultado: OK.

body:
## Summary

- **Tail-read transcript**: Seek to last 100KB of JSONL instead of parsing the entire file. Eliminates statusline flashing during heavy tool execution on large transcripts.
- **Fixed line-count padding**: Always output `getMaxLines()` lines with NBSP padding, preventing ghost/stale lines when activity lines appear or disappear.
- **Parallelize git calls**: Run `rev-parse`, `status --porcelain`, and `rev-list` concurrently via `Promise.all` (~2x faster).
- **Cache countConfigs**: 30s TTL file-based cache for MCP/rules/hooks/CLAUDE.md counts, avoiding repeated disk scans every 300ms cycle.
- **Cache loadConfig**: 30s TTL + mtime invalidation for HUD config, skipping redundant JSON parsing.
- **Skip idle speed-tracker writes**: Only write cache when output token count changes (~90% fewer disk writes during idle).

## Trade-offs

- `sessionStart` from transcript may be approximate for sessions exceeding 100KB of JSONL (tail-read starts mid-file). Duration display will show time since the tail window, not true session start.
- `getMaxLines()` slightly over-reserves lines (safe direction — extra blank padding rather than ghost lines).

## Test plan

- [x] Build passes (`npm run build`)

author: pedrosanzmtz
body:
## Summary

- Add `rounding` parameter (`"nearest"` | `"floor"`) to `get_elevation()` and `get_elevations_batch()` in the Python bindings for srtm.py-compatible grid cell selection
- Add `get_elevation_floor()` and `get_elevations_batch_floor()` methods to the Rust `SrtmTile` and `SrtmService` APIs
- Bump htg and htg-python to v0.3.4

## Details

srtm.py uses `math.floor()` for row/column index calculation (southwest-biased), while htg uses `round()` (true nearest-neighbor). This causes 1-3 meter differences at grid cell boundaries, breaking exact-value migration tests.

The new `rounding="floor"` option enables exact parity with srtm.py:

```python
# Default behavior (unchanged)
service.get_elevation(33.3448, -96.1592)  # 190 (nearest)

# srtm.py-compatible
service.get_elevation(33.3448, -96.1592, rounding="floor")  # 191 (floor)
```

Internally, `SrtmTile::get_elevation()` and `get_elevation_floor()` share logic via `get_elevation_inner()` with a configurable rounding function pointer, keeping the implementation DRY.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_floor_vs_round_different_results` — verifies floor and round select different grid cells for the example coordinate from the issue
- [x] `test_floor_matches_round_at_exact_grid` — verifies floor and round agree at exact grid points
- [x] `test_get_elevation_floor` — service-level floor query
- [x] `test_get_elevation_floor_missing_tile` — returns None for missing tiles
- [x] `test_get_elevations_batch_floor` — batch floor queries
- [x] All 81 existing tests continue to pass

Closes #68

### Motivation
- Polymarket Gamma responses and result ordering varied in the wild causing the bot to miss active BTC up/down markets (visible on site but not discovered by the bot). 
- The runtime assumed hardcoded 15m windows which prevented correct anchoring/candles/entry timing when only 5m markets were live. 

### Description
- Increased Gamma discovery pagination to scan up to `30` pages of `200` results each and added offset paging to avoid missing markets deep in the active list (`core/polymarket_client.py`).
- Hardened Gamma payload parsing by supporting both `token_id` and `tokenId`, falling back to `liquidityNum`/`volumeNum` when `liquidityClob`/`volume` are absent, and de-duplicating by `conditionId` (`core/polymarket_client.py`).
- Added clearer runtime logging for market discovery so the cycle distinguishes `no markets discovered` vs `markets discovered but none met liquidity threshold` (`bot.py`).
- Made the bot interval-aware: added interval inference from market slug/question, an interval refresh routine that auto-switches between 15m/5m (or the smallest available), parameterized anchor/candle fetches to use the active interval, and adjusted boundary calculations and entry timing to honor the active interval (`bot.py`, `oracles/price_feed.py`).
- Minor UX and dashboard changes to expose live/current bankroll and update README wording to reflect auto 5m/15m behavior (`core/dashboard_server.py`, `README.md`).

The util `function touchScrollInTarget` aims to touch scroll the target smoothly. However, currently it creates **accelerating** scrolling: as the coordinates of `target` keep changing during the touch move which we use as origin. This is not intended.

body:
Fixes #17603. Memory flush prompts include a literal `YYYY-MM-DD` placeholder (e.g. `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`). Without a reliable date in context, models can guess the wrong year. This PR resolves the placeholder before invoking the embedded agent, using the configured user timezone (falling back to UTC). It also adds a small helper `formatUserDateYmd` and a unit test. Notes: - I did not run the full test suite locally (node_modules not installed in this environment); changes are small and covered by a new unit test file.

Greptile Summary

This PR bundles three independent fixes: 1. **Memory flush YYYY-MM-DD placeholder resolution** (`agent-runner-memory.ts`, `date-time.ts`, `date-time.test.ts`): Resolves the literal `YYYY-MM-DD` placeholder in memory flush prompts before invoking the embedded agent, using the user's configured timezone. Adds a well-tested `formatUserDateYmd` helper that uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `en-CA` locale for reliable YYYY-MM-DD output. This is the core fix for #17603. 2. **Systemd user bus early guard** (`lifecycle.ts`): Adds early `isSystemdUserServiceAvailable()` checks in `runDaemonStart`, `runDaemonStop`, and `runDaemonRestart` to prevent `service.isLoaded()` from throwing on Linux systems without a systemd user bus. Returns gracefully with hints instead. 3. **`.venv` in skills watcher ignore list** (`refresh.ts`): Prevents Python virtual environments from triggering unnecessary skill reloads. - The memory flush fix is clean and follows existing codebase patterns for timezone resolution. - The `runDaemonStop` systemd guard computes `hints` but doesn't include them in the JSON emit (unlike `start`/`restart`) — minor inconsistency flagged.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk; the core date placeholder fix is correct and well-tested. - The memory flush YYYY-MM-DD fix is clean, well-tested, and follows existing codebase patterns. The systemd early guard and .venv ignore are low-risk additions. One minor inconsistency: `runDaemonStop` doesn't pass hints to the JSON emit unlike the other two lifecycle functions. Score is 4 rather than 5 because the PR bundles three unrelated changes (per CLAUDE.md: "Group related changes; avoid bundling unrelated refactors") and the author notes they did not run the full test suite locally. - Pay close attention to `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts` for the `runDaemonStop` hints inconsistency with `runDaemonStart` and `runDaemonRestart`. author: youngjoon-lee
body:
## 1. What does this PR implement?

This PR removes `wait_until_services_are_ready!` from the API service.

Previously, API service was waiting for Network, Storage, Mempool, Chain, and ChainLeader service. But, the ChainLeader service becomes ready only after the chain enters the Online mode. It takes time depending on [IBD and PBP](https://www.notion.so/nomos-tech/Cryptarchia-v1-Bootstrapping-Synchronization-1fd261aa09df81ac94b5fb6a4eff32a6?source=copy_link#1fd261aa09df8113baa7c8c751f7d8e3). Because of that, we were not able to use basic APIs (e.g. `cryptarchia/info`) during the chain Bootstrapping mode. 

To fix it, we now do not wait for service dependencies. API service becomes ready immediately. Instead, we rely on the [timeout middleware](https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-blockchain/blob/4b481023e3c1753da5b226b54c22200fbfa6f56e/nodes/node/binary/src/api/backend.rs#L281) we've already had. The API service tries to send a request to the other service via the Overwatch relay, regardless of whether it is ready or not. If it is failed to send a request in time, or if the service didn't respond in time, the API service returns `408: Request Timeout` to the end user.

The video below shows this scenario. I set 20s to PBP and 3s to API timeout. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2dcd0a4c-4d59-4cc2-807c-570e9f69c38e


### Future work

In a next PR, we can probably improve API service to introduce the on-demand service dependency check. 
Now that we are not waiting for service dependencies, the request messages will be stacked on the Overwatch relay (with buffer=16 hardcoded). It is not an issue for immutable operations (e.g. GET) but may be little tricky for POST operations.

For example, if a user calls `POST /leader/claim` during bootstrapping, the request will be timed out but will be stuck in the relay. Once the ChainLeader becomes ready, it will read the request from the relay, process it, and tries to send the response back. Sending the response will be failed because `oneshot::Sender` is already dropped by the requester. But, the ChainLeader already claimed the leader reward by processing the request. 

I believe this is not a big issue, because afaik, it's fine that a request is processed by the server, even if the user gets a timeout error, as long as the server state is consistent. But, I'm just mentioning that we can consider an improvement: We can check whether service dependencies are ready whenever we process an API request, and can return `503 Service Unavailable` (or any other) if they are not ready.

We can merge this PR first to unblock enabling IBD in devnet, and discuss about this improvement separately.

## 2. Does the code have enough context to be clearly understood?

I believe so

@youngjoon-lee

n/a

n/a

body:
### Motivation
- Async activations were returning ambiguous/partial diagnostics (e.g. `accepted=true` with `warnings=["diagnostics_partial"]`) and clients could observe null/partial schema on polling, breaking deterministic seed lineage and UI handling.
- Ensure async activation always publishes a clear lifecycle diagnostics record (`pending|ready|error`) with seed lineage so clients can render degraded-but-accepted states defensively.

### Description
- Reworked the async `POST /api/helix/time-dilation/activate` flow to immediately publish a `pending` diagnostics envelope and to atomically update `latestDiagnostics` to `ready` (full canonical diagnostics shape) or `error` on background completion/failure, and preserved `202 accepted` semantics.
- Updated `GET /api/helix/time-dilation/diagnostics` to return a deterministic envelope on `200` including `status`, `updatedAt`, `renderingSeed`, `seedStatus`, `reason`, and `payload` (no ambiguous null payloads).
- Added client-side parsing utility `parseActivateContract` and updated UI to surface a non-blocking "Diagnostics partial" badge with canonical context when `diagnostics_partial` is present.
- Added startup config resolution (`server/startup-config.ts`) and hardened several client hooks (`use-energy-pipeline`, `useGrConstraintContract`, `useProofPack`) with gateway-backoff handling; added unit/integration tests to cover pending/ready/error diagnostics and seed lineage.

### Testing
- Ran targeted Vitest suite including `tests/time-dilation-activate.spec.ts` plus other integration suites (total shown in run): 19 test files, 94 tests — all passed (no failing tests).
- Manual endpoint validation against a local server confirmed deterministic `pending` activate response and explicit diagnostics `ready|error` envelopes (one follow-up diagnostics poll hit a local timeout under heavy GR load but contract/metadata remained explicit).
- Adapter verification: `POST /api/agi/adapter/run` => verdict `PASS`, certificate hash `d2821c7d650d8d4c86f5270c2510b94ed7cd8c45b12d807e0420613f9fe7ce5d`, `integrityOk: true`.

author: samggreenberg
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the clip sorting and selection workflow by introducing threshold-based classification and intelligent clip selection strategies. It adds Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) thresholding for text-based sorting and implements cross-calibration for more robust threshold estimation in learned sorting.

## Key Changes

- **GMM-based Thresholding**: Added `calculate_gmm_threshold()` function that uses a 2-component Gaussian Mixture Model to automatically identify the boundary between "good" and "bad" clips based on score distributions. Falls back to median if GMM fitting fails.

- **Cross-Calibration Training**: Implemented `calculate_cross_calibration_threshold()` that splits training data into two halves, trains separate models on each, and computes thresholds on held-out data for more robust threshold estimation.

- **Refactored Model Training**: Extracted model training logic into `train_model()` function to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability.

- **Optimal Threshold Finding**: Added `find_optimal_threshold()` to compute the threshold that maximizes classification accuracy on labeled data.

- **Enhanced API Responses**: Modified `/api/sort` and `/api/learned-sort` endpoints to return both results and computed thresholds in a structured format: `{"results": [...], "threshold": ...}`.

- **UI Improvements**:
  - Added "Select" mode toggle with "Good" (highest scoring) and "Hard" (closest to threshold) options
  - Added "Next Clip" button for intelligent clip selection based on the selected mode
  - Display threshold percentage in the sort status
  - Improved sort bar layout with labels

- **Updated Tests**: Modified all test cases to account for the new response structure with nested `results` field and added assertions for threshold presence.

## Implementation Details

- The cross-calibration approach trains two independent models on different data splits and averages their thresholds, reducing overfitting to a single threshold estimate
- The "Hard" selection mode helps identify uncertain/boundary cases by selecting clips closest to the decision threshold, useful for active learning scenarios
- All threshold values are rounded to 4 decimal places for consistency with score formatting

body:
This pull request finalizes the migration of the LoanBroker showcase from AWS to Azure, upgrading the entire system to .NET 10 and NServiceBus 10, and ensuring all services run locally in Docker containers with Azure-equivalent infrastructure. Comprehensive documentation has been added and updated to reflect the new architecture, setup, and operational procedures. The changes make the project production-ready, developer-friendly, and fully observable with modern monitoring tools.

**Key changes include:**

### Migration Completion & Documentation

- Added `MIGRATION_COMPLETE.md`, providing a detailed summary of the migration, including technical achievements, migration goals vs. results, final statistics, lessons learned, performance metrics, and knowledge transfer notes.
- Added `MIGRATION_PLAN.md`, outlining the migration phases, AWS-to-Azure service mapping, deliverables, prerequisites, and success criteria for the transition.
- Created a comprehensive `README-SETUP.md` with step-by-step setup, troubleshooting, architecture decisions, and performance expectations for the new Azure-based system.

### Main README and Usage Updates

- Updated `README.md` to reflect the migration to Azure, including new quick start instructions, updated requirements, and revised architecture descriptions.
- Revised the monitoring and requirements sections in `README.md` to reference Azure-native infrastructure (Azure Service Bus Emulator, SQL Server, OpenTelemetry collector) and updated the quick start instructions for both Windows and Linux/Mac environments.

These changes collectively mark the successful modernization of the LoanBroker showcase, making it easier to develop, run, and monitor locally with no cloud dependencies.

author: quietsignal44
body:
## Summary
- Adds `Referer` header to `search.headers` for the Gay-Torrents.net indexer definition
- Fixes torrent downloads returning 0 bytes

## Problem
Gay-Torrents.net requires a `Referer` header on download requests. Without it, the server returns HTTP 200 with **0 bytes** instead of the actual `.torrent` file.

The Cardigann engine falls back to `search.headers` for download requests when no `download:` block is defined (`Definition.Download?.Headers ?? Definition.Search?.Headers`), so adding the header here covers both search and download.

## Testing
- Verified via direct HTTP requests that GET to the download URL **without** `Referer` returns 0 bytes
- Verified that GET to the download URL **with** `Referer` returns a valid `.torrent` file
- Any `Referer` value works, but using the site's own URL is the correct approach

body:
This pull request adds robust CLI support for converting Excel files to CSV, introduces a dedicated XLSX-to-CSV conversion module, and significantly improves test coverage for both CLI argument parsing and Excel data conversion. The changes also refactor the main process to use the new module for both CLI and GUI operations, and remove now-redundant conversion logic from the main file.

**Major improvements include:**

### CLI Support and Argument Parsing

* Added a new `parseCliArgs` function and CLI help text in `cli-args.js`, enabling command-line usage for Excel-to-CSV conversion with clear error handling and help output.
* Integrated CLI mode handling into `main.js`, allowing the app to run in CLI mode (`--xlsx ... --out ...`), display help, or show errors, and exit accordingly.

### XLSX-to-CSV Conversion Refactor

* Extracted and enhanced all Excel-to-CSV conversion logic into a new `xlsx-converter.js` module, including robust header normalization, summary row filtering, blank date filling, and CSV escaping. This module is now used by both CLI and GUI code paths.
* Updated the GUI's file reading logic in `main.js` to delegate XLSX conversion to the new module, removing the previous inline implementation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bc7c8961bc09bec195b82efba11db117900b0e7348f81bc5d8868db65f783e80L130-R157) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bc7c8961bc09bec195b82efba11db117900b0e7348f81bc5d8868db65f783e80L159-L180)

### Test Coverage

* Added comprehensive tests for CLI argument parsing in `cli-args.test.js`, covering all main code paths (no args, help, error, and valid conversion).
* Added thorough tests for Excel conversion in `xlsx-converter.test.js`, validating header extraction, summary row filtering, blank date filling, and correct CSV output for various edge cases.

author: copilot
body:
`@object-ui/fields` provides 36 field widgets but the designer components expose only a fraction of them. This adds a comprehensive evaluation (Section 10) to the design doc covering the gap and integration path.

### Field Type Inventory (10.2)
- Full catalog of all 36 field types across 8 categories (text, numeric, datetime, selection, contact, file, location, computed, complex)
- Cross-referenced against type interfaces, cell renderers, form mappers, and current designer availability

### Gap Analysis (10.3)
- **DataModelDesigner**: No field type selector UI — new fields hardcoded to `'text'`, `DataModelField.type` is generic `string` not a union
- **PageDesigner**: `DEFAULT_PALETTE` has 14 generic items (e.g. `input`, `checkbox`) instead of leveraging the 36 `@object-ui/fields` widgets
- **ViewDesigner**: Plain text type badges, no icons/categorization

### Proposed `DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES` Constant (10.4)
Centralized field type registry with Lucide icons, categories, and descriptions for use across all designers:

```typescript
export const DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES: DesignerFieldTypeOption[] = [
  { type: 'text', label: 'Text', icon: Type, category: 'text', description: 'Single-line text input' },
  { type: 'currency', label: 'Currency', icon: Hash, category: 'number', description: 'Monetary value with currency symbol' },
  // ... all 36 types
];
```

### Type Safety Recommendations (10.6)
- Extract `FieldTypeName` from the `FieldMetadata` union discriminant
- Update `DataModelField.type` from `string` → `FieldTypeName`
- Complete `mapFieldTypeToFormType` for missing 9 types

### Integration Plan & Phasing (10.5, 10.7)
Per-designer implementation points with P0–P3 prioritization, estimated at 7–9.5 dev-days total.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a practical MINCO-style quintic polynomial optimizer to replace the previous placeholder and enable phased migration from B-spline to MINCO while keeping the existing execution pipeline working. 
- Ensure trajectories are conservative with a duration heuristic derived from distance, max velocity and max acceleration to avoid infeasible (too aggressive) segments.

### Description

- Add a new `minco_opt` package (`CMakeLists.txt`, `package.xml`, `include/minco_opt/minco_optimizer.h`, `src/minco_optimizer.cpp`) implementing `MincoOptimizer` that solves quintic coefficients (`c3,c4,c5`) and outputs ascending coefficients (`c0..c5`) and durations. 
- Integrate MINCO into the planner by adding `manager/use_minco` param and `use_minco` flag in `PlanParameters`, include and initialize `MincoOptimizer` in `planner_manager`, and in `reboundReplan` sample MINCO segments into points, convert them to `UniformBspline` control points, and fall back to the original bspline optimizer on failure. 
- Add local helper evaluators for MINCO polynomials (`evalMincoPoly`, `evalMincoDeriv`, `evalMincoAcc`) and wire up conversions and start/end derivative extraction for Bspline parameterization. 
- Add `docs/minco_replacement_guide.md` with migration guidance and make ancillary build updates (add `minco_opt` dependency to `plan_manage` CMake/package files, adjust `multi_map_server` `add_dependencies` invocation, and improve CUDA option handling in `local_sensing/CMakeLists.txt`).

### Testing

- Displayed and inspected the implemented source with `nl -ba src/planner/minco_opt/src/minco_optimizer.cpp` which succeeded.

author: hakuturu583
body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
1. **Missing OpenDRIVE standard attribute**: Added missing `rule` attribute to road element and fixed incorrect placement on lane elements

---

## 🔍 Root Cause Analysis

### Problem Description
The ASAM OpenDRIVE specification defines an optional `rule` attribute for the `<road>` element to specify the traffic rule (right-hand traffic or left-hand traffic). The implementation had two issues:

1. **Missing implementation**: The `rule` attribute was not being set on `Road` objects during construction
2. **Incorrect placement**: The `rule` attribute was being output on `<lane>` elements instead of `<road>` elements, violating the OpenDRIVE standard

### Technical Details
According to the ASAM OpenDRIVE specification, the `rule` attribute:
- Type: `e_trafficRule` (enumeration)
- Values: `RHT` (right-hand traffic) or `LHT` (left-hand traffic)
- Optional attribute with RHT as the default when omitted
- **Must be placed on the `<road>` element, not `<lane>` elements**
- Defines the basic rule for using the road

The original implementation incorrectly passed `traffic_rule` to individual lanes and output the attribute on `<lane>` elements, which is non-standard behavior.

---

## 🛠️ Changes

### 1. TrafficRule Enum (enums.py)
**Added missing enum for OpenDRIVE traffic rule standard**

```python
# After: TrafficRule enum per OpenDRIVE standard
class TrafficRule(Enum):
    """Traffic rule according to OpenDRIVE standard (e_trafficRule)."""

    RHT = "RHT"  # Right-hand traffic
    LHT = "LHT"  # Left-hand traffic
```

### 2. Road Class (road.py)
**Added missing rule attribute to Road dataclass**

```python
# Before: Road missing standard attribute
@dataclass
class Road:
    id: int = 0
    name: Optional[str] = None
    length: float = 0.0
    junction: int = -1
    # ... other attributes

# After: Road with standard-compliant rule attribute
@dataclass
class Road:
    id: int = 0
    name: Optional[str] = None
    length: float = 0.0
    junction: int = -1
    rule: Optional[TrafficRule] = None  # Added missing attribute
    # ... other attributes
```

### 3. XML Generation (road.py)
**Updated to_xml() to output rule attribute per standard**

```python
# After: Rule attribute added to XML output
def to_xml(self) -> ET.Element:
    elem = ET.Element("road")
    elem.set("id", str(self.id))
    elem.set("length", str(self.length))
    elem.set("junction", str(self.junction))

    if self.name:
        elem.set("name", self.name)

    if self.rule:  # Added: Output rule attribute
        elem.set("rule", self.rule.value)
    
    # ... rest of the method
```

### 4. Road Construction (road.py)
**Fixed: Set rule attribute when constructing roads from lanelets**

```python
# Added: Convert traffic_rule string to TrafficRule enum
rule_enum = None
if traffic_rule:
    traffic_rule_normalized = traffic_rule.upper()
    if traffic_rule_normalized == "RHT":
        rule_enum = TrafficRule.RHT
    elif traffic_rule_normalized == "LHT":
        rule_enum = TrafficRule.LHT

road = Road(
    id=road_id,
    name=f"Road_{road_id}",
    length=road_length,
    junction=-1,
    rule=rule_enum,  # Now correctly set
    # ... other attributes
)
```

### 5. Lane Section (lane_section.py)
**Fixed: Removed incorrect rule parameter passing to lanes**

```python
# Before: Incorrectly passing rule to lane elements
lane = Lane.construct_from_lanelet(
    lanelet_map, lanelet, rule=traffic_rule, width_config=width_config
)

# After: No longer passing rule to lanes
lane = Lane.construct_from_lanelet(
    lanelet_map, lanelet, width_config=width_config
)
```

---

## ✅ Testing

Pre-commit checks:
- [x] ruff (linting)
- [x] ruff-format (formatting)
- [x] mypy (type checking)
- [x] pytest (unit tests)

Manual testing:
- [x] All pre-commit hooks passed successfully
- [x] Type checking confirms proper integration with existing code
- [x] Verified generated OpenDRIVE XML output

### Output Verification

**Before (incorrect):**
```xml
<road id="0" length="15.390938860426228" junction="-1" name="Road_0">
  <lanes>
    <laneSection s="0.0">
      <left>
        <lane id="1" type="driving" level="false" rule="LHT">
```

**After (correct):**
```xml
<road id="0" length="15.390938860426228" junction="-1" name="Road_0" rule="LHT">
  <lanes>
    <laneSection s="0.0">
      <left>
        <lane id="1" type="driving" level="false">
```

---

## 📊 Expected Results

After merging this PR:
- ✅ Generated OpenDRIVE files properly support the standard `rule` attribute on `<road>` elements
- ✅ `rule` attribute is no longer incorrectly placed on `<lane>` elements
- ✅ Full compliance with ASAM OpenDRIVE specification for road elements
- ✅ Backward compatible - existing code continues to work without modification (rule is optional)
- ✅ Type-safe implementation using enum prevents invalid values

---

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

**None**

This change is fully backward compatible. The `rule` attribute is optional per the OpenDRIVE standard, and existing code that does not set this attribute will continue to work as before.

---

## 📝 Related Issues

Fixes incomplete OpenDRIVE standard compliance for traffic rule specification.

## Summary

Fixes #158 and #159.

- **#158 (atomicity)**: Resolution decision creation + conflict status update now happen in a single transaction. Previously two separate transactions — a crash between them would leave an orphaned resolution decision and an unresolved conflict. Extracted `createTraceInTx` from `CreateTraceTx` and added `CreateTraceAndResolveConflictTx`. Refactored `service.Trace` into `prepareTrace` + `postTraceAsync` so the new `ResolveConflictWithTrace` reuses all preparation and post-commit logic without duplication.

- **#159 (audit gaps)**: `ReviseDecision` now accepts an optional `*MutationAuditEntry` inserted atomically in the same transaction as the revision. `ResolveOrCreateAgent` now accepts an optional audit entry and uses `CreateAgentWithAudit` for auto-registered agents, making auto-registration visible in the audit trail. Both HTTP and MCP callers pass audit context.

## Changes

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `internal/storage/trace.go` | Extract `createTraceInTx`, add `CreateTraceAndResolveConflictTx` + `ResolveConflictInTraceParams` |
| `internal/storage/decisions.go` | Add optional `*MutationAuditEntry` to `ReviseDecision` |
| `internal/service/decisions/service.go` | Extract `prepareTrace`/`postTraceAsync`, add `ResolveConflictWithTrace`, add audit param to `ResolveOrCreateAgent` |

body:
Added a `colorScheme` prop to the `StackNavigation` component to support both "neutral" (default) and "primary" color schemes. This change addresses the issue where stack navigation was using primary colors by default, while neutral colors are used more frequently in the codebase.

### Changes

### src/components/ui/stack-navigation.tsx

- **Added `colorScheme` prop** with two options: `"neutral"` (default) and `"primary"`
- **Refactored to use `class-variance-authority` (cva)** pattern, matching the button component implementation for consistency
- **Created `stackNavigationItemVariants`** using cva with:
  - `orientation` variant (vertical/horizontal)
  - `colorScheme` variant (neutral/primary)
  - `isActive` variant (true/false)
  - Compound variants for all combinations
- **Implemented color states** for both schemes:
  - **Neutral**: Text always `neutral-fg`, background transitions: none → `neutral-bg` (hover) → `neutral-200` (pressing) → `neutral-bg` (active)
  - **Primary**: Text `neutral-fg` (default/hover) → `primary-fg` (pressing/active), background: none → `neutral-bg` (hover) → `primary-bg` (pressing/active)
- **Exported variants** for reuse: `stackNavigationItemVariants` and `StackNavigationItemVariants` type

### `registries/registry.json`
- Added `"class-variance-authority"` to dependencies array for stack-navigation component

### Demo Files

- **Updated main demo** (`src/app/content/ui/stack-navigation.tsx`): Added `colorScheme="neutral"` prop
- **Updated horizontal demo** (`src/app/content/ui/stack-navigation-horizontal.tsx`): Added `colorScheme="neutral"` prop
- **Created new color schemes demo** (`src/app/content/ui/stack-navigation-color-schemes.tsx`): Side-by-side comparison of both color schemes
- **Updated usage examples** (`src/app/demo/[name]/ui/stack-navigation.tsx`): Added examples showing both colorScheme options

- Fix the 422 Unprocessable Content when n8n calls `POST /generar-cotizacion` by aligning the API contract with the JSON n8n sends.
- Accept `selections` as a list of items and `customer` as an object while preserving existing behavior for legacy fields. 
- Keep changes minimal and backward-compatible so old callers using `modelo`, `nombre_cliente`, etc., keep working.

### Description
- Updated the FastAPI request model in `fastapi_app.py` to include `SelectionItem` and `Customer` types and accept `machine`, `basePrice`, `totalPrice`, `selections: list|dict` and `customer: object|string` while preserving `extra="allow"` and legacy fields.

- Adjusted pricing flow in `cotizador_backend.py` to accept optional `precio_base_override` and `precio_total_override` (fed from `basePrice`/`totalPrice`) so payload-provided base/total are honored while preserving legacy calculation when absent. 
- Improved model normalization in `template_resolver.py` to strip `.docx`, whitespace and normalize case so `CM640`, `cm 640` and `CM640.docx` resolve to the same template, and updated `README.md` with a manual `uvicorn` + `curl`/PowerShell example showing the n8n payload.

body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `getUserIdFromAuth` helper function manually decoded JWTs from the `Authorization` header without verifying the signature. This allowed an attacker to forge a token with any user ID and impersonate any user on endpoints like `POST /api/comments`.
🎯 Impact: Complete account takeover and unauthorized actions (create/delete/modify comments, likes, reports) on affected endpoints.
🔧 Fix: Replaced the insecure manual JWT decoding with `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()`, which leverages Convex Auth's built-in secure verification. Removed the vulnerable helper function.
✅ Verification: Ran `pnpm eslint` and `pnpm test`. Verified manually that the insecure function is removed and replaced with standard `ctx.auth` calls.

author: arjenschwarz
body:
## Summary

- Fix cross-context SwiftData relationship issue causing comments to not appear immediately after creation
- `CommentService.addComment()` now re-fetches the task in its own `ModelContext` before establishing the relationship, ensuring the comment is immediately queryable
- Fix pre-existing whitespace-only comment bug in `TaskService.updateStatus()` that could roll back status changes
- Refactor `AddCommentIntent` to expose a testable `execute()` method (matching all other intents), fixing a pre-existing test compilation error

## Root Cause

`TransitApp.init()` creates a separate `ModelContext` for services, distinct from `container.mainContext` used by `@Query`. When the view passes a task from `@Query` to `CommentService.addComment()`, the `Comment` was created with a cross-context relationship. SwiftData does not resolve cross-context relationships immediately, so `fetchComments()` could not find the newly inserted comment until contexts auto-merged.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test `addComment_taskFromDifferentContext_immediatelyFetchable` verifies cross-context comment creation
- [x] Full test suite passes (624 tests, 0 failures)
- [x] SwiftLint passes (0 violations)
- [ ] Manual: Add a comment in task detail view and verify it appears immediately

author: lgkeroack
body:
This task enhances the terrain rendering quality in the airspace graph (3D route visualization) to provide more accurate and detailed representation of land topography under flight paths. The current implementation produces overly smooth terrain that does not accurately represent the actual land features due to a combination of low-resolution elevation data (SRTM 30-90m), additional smoothing algorithms applied during rendering, and sparse sampling (500m cell size). The goal is to increase terrain fidelity by improving data resolution, reducing artificial smoothing, and increasing point density.

- Added frames-per-second (FPS) performance counter in development mode for monitoring rendering efficiency
- Implemented intelligent, route-length-aware sampling that automatically adapts resolution based on route distance, optimizing both visual quality and performance
- Enhanced terrain rendering with improved detail preservation and refined processing parameters for routes of all lengths

## Summary
- `documents_fts` is an FTS5 virtual table, not a column on `documents`

body:
The AI system components (providers, tools, memory, reasoning modes) were not automatically initialized or validated on startup. This resulted in silent failures and no visibility into system readiness.

## Changes

### Core Implementation
- **`AIInitializer`** (`backend/src/ai/core/ai-initializer.ts`)
  - Validates provider config (OpenAI/Anthropic) and API keys
  - Initializes tool registry, memory system, reasoning modes
  - Reports status with errors/warnings, continues on non-critical failures
  - Singleton pattern with idempotent initialization

### Integration
- **Server startup** (`backend/src/server.ts`)
  ```typescript
  // Before: manual, incomplete
  if (process.env.FEATURE_AI_CORE === 'true') {
    initializeTools();
  }
  
  // After: comprehensive, automatic
  await AIInitializer.initialize();
  ```

- **Status endpoint** (`backend/src/routes/ai.ts`)
  - `GET /api/ai/status` - public health check for monitoring
  - Returns: `{ enabled, healthy, provider, toolsAvailable, reasoningModes, initialized }`

### Testing
- Test script validates all components: `npm run test:autorun`
- Verifies graceful degradation with missing API keys

### Observability
Console output shows initialization progress:
```
🚀 Starting AI system initialization...
✅ AI Provider initialized: openai
✅ Tool registry initialized with 1 tools
✅ Memory system initialized
✅ Reasoning modes available: 10
⚠️  Warnings: AI provider not configured - missing API keys
```

## Security
- API keys validated but never exposed in responses
- No actual provider calls during init (avoids costs/unauthorized usage)
- CodeQL scan: 0 vulnerabilities

**WebSocket resiliency (9.5/10)**
- Exponential backoff with 80-120% jitter prevents thundering herd
- Automatic 2s fallback polling when WebSocket unavailable
- Clean lifecycle: handler de-registration, null checks
- Event normalization handles multiple envelope formats (`economy.agent`, `agent_update`)

**Test quality (8.5/10)**
- 91.98% coverage, 192/192 tests passing
- Focused unit tests per module + integration test for incremental redraw
- Clean WebSocket mock with realistic behavior

body:
## Summary

- Add header-based dimension check in `sanitize()` for the lazy decode path (`fromPath()`)
- When the image is not yet decoded, read the header to extract dimensions and run `enforce_pixels()` against the firewall policy
- This ensures consistent early rejection for both `from(buffer)` and `fromPath(path)` construction paths

**Before**: `fromPath(oversized).sanitize({ policy: 'strict' })` would succeed at `sanitize()` time and only fail at encode time
**After**: `fromPath(oversized).sanitize({ policy: 'strict' })` fails immediately at `sanitize()` time, matching `from(buffer)` behavior

## Test plan

- [x] New test: `enforce_pixels_rejects_oversized_image_from_header` — header-based check catches oversized images
- [x] New test: `enforce_pixels_allows_small_image_from_header` — small images pass correctly
- [x] All 359 existing Rust tests pass (`cargo test --no-default-features`)
- [ ] CI: verify JS integration tests with both `from()` and `fromPath()` paths

This PR establishes the i18n foundation and provides a complete Chinese translation, making opcode accessible to Chinese-speaking developers. ## What's included ### Infrastructure - `src/i18n/index.ts` — i18next config with `LanguageDetector` (auto-detects browser locale, persists choice to localStorage) - `src/i18n/locales/en.json` — English translation keys extracted from source - `src/i18n/locales/zh-CN.json` — Simplified Chinese translations - `src/components/LanguageSwitcher.tsx` — Dropdown component for switching languages ### Converted components (as examples) | Component | Scope | |-----------|-------| | `CustomTitlebar.tsx` | Tooltip labels, dropdown menu items | | `ProjectList.tsx` | All user-facing strings (title, buttons, empty state) | | `Topbar.tsx` | Status indicator, version display, install prompts | | `Settings.tsx` | Header, 8 tab labels, all form labels/descriptions, toast messages, permission rules | ### Translation conventions | English | Chinese | Rationale | |---------|---------|-----------| | Agent | 智能体 | Standard AI term in Chinese (not 代理) | | Checkpoint | 检查点 | | | Token | Token | Industry standard, kept as-is | | Claude Code / opcode | Claude Code / opcode | Brand names, kept as-is | | Hook | 钩子 | | | MCP | MCP (模型上下文协议) | Abbreviation + full name | ### How to convert remaining components The pattern is straightforward — each component just needs: ```tsx import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"; // Inside the component: const { t } = useTranslation(); // Replace hardcoded text: // Before:

Projects

// After:

{t("projects.title")}

// With interpolation: // Before: View all ({count}) // After: {t("projects.viewAll", { count })} ``` The remaining ~50 components can be converted incrementally in follow-up PRs. ## Dependencies added - `i18next` — Core i18n framework - `react-i18next` — React bindings - `i18next-browser-languagedetector` — Auto-detect user's browser language ## Test plan - [ ] App starts without errors with default English locale - [ ] Switching to zh-CN via globe icon in titlebar changes all converted component text to Chinese - [ ] Language preference persists across app restarts (stored in localStorage) - [ ] Settings page tab labels, form labels, and toast messages display correctly in both languages - [ ] ProjectList empty state, headers, and buttons display correctly in both languages - [ ] Topbar version status and install prompts display correctly in both languages - [ ] TypeScript compilation passes (`tsc --noEmit`)

body:
## Scope
Implement deterministic provenance ordering and deduplication in `runWithEvidence`, with replay fixtures covering citation duplication behavior.

## Motivation
LlamaIndex users report duplicated citations under chunking configurations (`https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/17439`). This change makes extraction ordering and dedup deterministic for identical spans across chunk layouts.

## Changes
- Runtime: `src/engine/run.ts`
  - Added stable extraction ordering by `(charStart, charEnd, extractionClass, quote, grounding, attributes)`.
  - Added deterministic identity-key dedup over extracted evidence records.
  - Applied ordering + dedup before final bundle emission.
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/provenance-dedup-replays.json`
  - Added replay fixture with source URL and chunk-config pairs reproducing duplicate-span behavior.
- Tests: `tests/engine/provenance-dedup-and-stability.test.ts`
  - Added exactly 2 tests for ordering determinism and dedup determinism.
- Wiring: `tests/run.ts`
  - Added import for `./engine/provenance-dedup-and-stability.test.ts`.

Role 1 — Builder
- Implemented runtime fix, replay fixture, tests, and test wiring.
- Verified formatting and full matrix pass.

Role 3 — Minimalism Reviewer
- `git diff --stat`:
  - `src/engine/run.ts | 74 +...-`
  - `tests/run.ts | 1 +`
  - `tests/engine/provenance-dedup-and-stability.test.ts | 232 +`
  - `tests/fixtures/provenance-dedup-replays.json | 11 +`
- Deleted files: none. Every introduced file directly supports deterministic provenance behavior or regression coverage.

## Verification
Commands executed locally:
- `npm run test:deno`
  - pass line: all tests completed with no failures.
- `npm run test:bun`
  - pass line: all tests completed with no failures.
- `npm run test:workers`
  - pass line: `ok - workers harness executes example worker and returns portability payload`.
- `npm run test:browser`
  - pass line: `ok - browser harness bundles browser example against built distribution`.
- `npm run bench`
  - pass line: `bench score passed ... successRate=1.0000 ... caseOutcomeDriftRate=0.0000`.
- `npm run check`
  - pass line: `repo-scope-check passed`, `repo-text-check passed`, and complete test suites passed.

Role 2 — Adversarial Reviewer
- Counterexample 1 encoded as test:
  - `provenance ordering is deterministic by global span and extraction identity`
  - Assertion that failed on `origin/main`: first extraction MUST be quote `Beta` with `charStart=6` even if provider output order is `Gamma` then `Beta`.
- Counterexample 2 encoded as test:
  - `provenance dedup is deterministic across chunk configurations for identical spans`
  - Assertions that failed on `origin/main`: each run MUST produce exactly one extraction for identical underlying span, and serialized extraction arrays MUST match across chunk configs.

## Evidence / Traceability
- Signal source used in fixture:
  - `https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/17439`
- Files:
  - `tests/fixtures/provenance-dedup-replays.json`
  - `tests/engine/provenance-dedup-and-stability.test.ts`
  - `src/engine/run.ts`

Role 4 — Release Auditor
- README/docs checked for stale process language; none added in this change.
- Forbidden token scans executed with zero matches:
  - `git grep -nE '\bPR-\d+\b|\bPR_\d+\b|\bPR \d+\b'`
  - `git grep -nE '\b(TODO|TBD|WIP)\b'`
  - `git grep -nEi 'public regression harness'`
  - `git grep -nE '\bWORKBENCH\b|\bPACK_ID\b|workbench pack'`

## Risk
- Risk: dedup identity key can collapse intentionally repeated extractions that are semantically distinct but byte-identical.
  - Mitigation: dedup key includes extraction class, grounding, and attributes in addition to span and quote.
- Risk: ordering key changes may alter snapshot order in downstream consumers.
  - Mitigation: ordering is deterministic and stable, and regression tests lock expected order.
- Risk: fixture drift can hide chunk-overlap behavior if chunk configuration is edited.
  - Mitigation: test asserts duplicate shard hits for both configs before final assertions.

## Rollback
1. Revert commit `feat(evidence): deterministic provenance ordering and dedup rules`.
2. Run full matrix in order:
   - `npm run test:deno`
   - `npm run test:bun`
   - `npm run test:workers`
   - `npm run test:browser`
   - `npm run bench`
   - `npm run check`

author: arockwell
body:
## Summary

Adds `emdx next` — a command that returns the single best next action for an AI agent.

- Outputs exactly one `emdx` command to **stdout** (machine-readable)
- Reasoning goes to **stderr** (human-readable)  
- Supports `--json` and `--verbose` flags

### Priority Logic

1. **In-progress tasks** → `emdx task view <id>` (finish what you started)
2. **Ready tasks** → `emdx task active <id>` (pick up unblocked work)
3. **Stale gameplans** (tagged `active` + `gameplan`, older than 7 days) → `emdx view <id>`
4. **Fallback** → `emdx prime`

### Files

- `emdx/commands/next.py` — New command implementation
- `emdx/main.py` — Register the command
- `tests/test_next.py` — 16 tests covering priority logic, query functions, and CLI output

### Usage

```bash
emdx next              # Print next action to stdout
emdx next --json       # JSON output with action, reasoning, priority
emdx next --verbose    # Detailed reasoning on stderr
eval $(emdx next)      # Execute the recommended action directly
```

## Summary

- **Root cause**: Each `network list` invocation created a new CDP connection and enabled `Network.enable`, but by the time it connected all requests had already completed — there was no retrospective way to get historical network data via CDP.
- **Fix**: `collect_and_correlate()` now triggers `Page.reload` after enabling the Network domain, subscribes to `Page.loadEventFired` as a completion signal, and waits for the page load event plus a short idle window for trailing async requests.
- **Regression tests**: Added BDD scenarios covering `network list`, `--type` filter, `--url` filter, `network get`, and `network follow` (unchanged behavior).

## Acceptance Criteria

From `.claude/specs/102-fix-network-list-empty-array/requirements.md`:

- [ ] AC1: `network list` returns captured requests after page load (non-empty JSON array with id, method, url, status, type)
- [ ] AC2: Type filter works (`--type document` returns only document-type requests)
- [ ] AC3: URL filter works (`--url "google"` returns only matching requests)
- [ ] AC4: `network get <id>` returns request details for captured requests
- [ ] AC5: `network follow` streaming still works (no regression)

## Test Plan

## Summary

Implements the complete Milestone 1 for Rubichan — a Go-based AI coding agent. This PR delivers the foundational architecture across 6 layers, 27 TDD tasks, and 31 commits.

### What's included

- **Config layer**: TOML loading with defaults, API key resolution from env/config sources
- **Provider layer**: Anthropic (Messages API) and OpenAI-compatible (Chat Completions) providers with SSE streaming, self-registration factory pattern
- **Tool layer**: File tool (read/write/patch with path traversal prevention), Shell tool (timeout + output truncation), interface-based registry
- **Agent core**: Conversation manager, context window manager (~4 chars/token heuristic), recursive turn loop with tool call execution and approval flow
- **TUI**: Bubble Tea model with slash commands (/quit, /clear, /model, /help), streaming display, lipgloss styling
- **CLI**: Cobra entrypoint with --config, --model, --provider flags, version subcommand
- **Integration test**: End-to-end smoke test verifying multi-turn file read/write flow
