author: jlaitine
body: ## Summary This PR fixes the following issues for the NXP93/NXP95 uSDHC driver: - The macros CONFIG_IMX9_USDHC_DMA and CONFIG_ARM64_DCACHE_DISABLE were mixed up a bit. All combinations of these macros should compile and work. - Some sdcards don't work with current board setups. The boards currently configure the cards to 50MHz, but this is really only supported if the card is set to either "high speed mode" at 3.3V, or some SDR25 or higher at 1.8V. This PR sets the SD card to high speed mode if the configured speed is above 25 MHz. - The bus speed configuration for boards is confusing, the boards directly define the prescalers and dividers, but root clocks are hidden in the driver. This PR allows configuring the wanted bus speed directly, and dividers are calculated by the driver - The root clock of the usdhc block was unnecesary low, but implementing the above allows easily increasing that. Now it is set to 400MHz, which is the nominal speed according to the iMX93 TRM. ## Impact This impacts imx9 architecture boards using SD cards / uSDHC driver, fixing stability issues ## Testing This is tested on i.MX93 EVK and with a custom i.MX93 board and with several SD cards (SanDisk, Kingston). Specifically "SanDisk 8GB Industrial XI" card is tested at most, since this card failed constantly when wrongly used with 50MHz bus without switching to high speed. The tests include: 1. Measured the frequencies with oscilloscope - Initialization frequency 400kHZ - 1-bit frequency 25 MHz - 4-bit high-speed frequency 50 MHz Here is one image, showing the 50MHz operation after card has been switched to HS mode. The red arrow shows the place where SOC writes to the card (data changes exactly at the falling edge). The blue arrow shows card writing to SoC, the data is set by the card 6ns after the clock rising edge. Before switch the data was set 6ns after the clock falling edge -> confirming that the switch was done successfully by the card. 2. Checked file system operation (there are much more real life testing with reading & writing, but this sanity check was done with also all the cache&dma combinations) ``` nsh> mount -t vfat /dev/mmcsd0 /fs/microsd nsh> cd /fs/microsd nsh> echo "Hello World!" > test.txt nsh> ls /fs/microsd: test.txt nsh> cat test.txt Hello World! ``` 3. Added debug code to dump the CMD6 response after the succesful HS switch (code uses bytes 12,13 and 16 acc. to the "SD Specifications Part 1 Physical Layer Simplified Specification" ``` imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 c8 80 01 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 80 01 80 01 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 80 01 c0 01 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 80 03 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 01 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 imx9_sdcard_hs_mode: 00 00 00 00 ``` 4. With a real application (px4, logger), wrote larger files (several MB each) to the card, and reading them back on PC and verifying the content. i.MX95 is not tested (I don't have the EVK), but this is essentially the same SoC regarding the uSD and clocking. It only has more cpu cores.

## Summary
This PR introduces significant improvements to the upload validation logic, implements timestamped naming for downloaded files, and performs a major cleanup of obsolete documentation. It also includes several UI/UX refinements across the converter and editor interfaces.

## Key Changes

### 🛠 Upload Validation & Documentation
- **Enhanced Validation**: Extensively refactored `upload-validator.ts` to enforce strict "Zero Tolerance" validation rules for single files, folders, and ZIP archives.
- **New Documentation**: Added [docs/upload-rules.md](cci:7://file:///home/nishan/Documents/markify-md-to-pdf-converter/docs/upload-rules.md:0:0-0:0) detailing the strict validation logic and success/failure scenarios.
- **Test Scenarios**: Generated comprehensive test scenarios to ensure the validation logic handles various edge cases correctly.

### 📄 File Management & Naming
- **Timestamped Downloads**: Implemented a new naming convention for exported PDFs and ZIP archives that includes timestamps.
- **Conditional Naming**: Added logic to [src/utils/naming.ts](cci:7://file:///home/nishan/Documents/markify-md-to-pdf-converter/src/utils/naming.ts:0:0-0:0) to apply these names based on the file's origin (Editor vs. Direct Upload).

### 🧹 Documentation Cleanup
- **Repository Optimization**: Deleted over 200 obsolete documentation files, setup checklists, and technical guides to reduce repository bloat and improve maintainability.

### ✨ UI/UX Refinements
- **Interactive Feedback**: Added `cursor-pointer` classes to `DropdownMenuItem` and file tree interactive elements for better visual feedback.
- **Landing Page Improvements**: Enhanced section extraction logic to better support page breaks and horizontal rule markers during PDF generation.
- **Client Components**: Updated `converter-client.tsx` and `editor-client.tsx` for more robust state handling and improved user flow.

### 🏗 Internal Services
- **Draft Management**: Introduced `draft-service.ts` and `draft-storage.ts` to improve the handling of transient file states and drafts.

## Impact
- **Reliability**: More robust upload processing with clear, documented rules.
- **Usability**: Improved file organization for users through timestamped downloads and better UI feedback.
- **Maintainability**: A significantly cleaner codebase and documentation structure.

## Verification Results
- Ran `git diff --stat` showing 211 files changed (1,228 insertions, 3,684 deletions).
- Verified validation logic against the new test scenarios defined in `docs/upload-rules.md`.

Adds a standalone web application for Firebase-powered key-value storage with authentication.

## Implementation

- **Authentication flow**: Sign up/in/out with localStorage-based session management

```javascript
const firebaseConfig = {
```

body:
Implements CfL prediction (Milestone 3 deliverable), which reduces chroma bitrate by exploiting luma-chroma correlation in DCT domain.

### Encoding pipeline changes (`VarDCTEncoder.swift`)

- **`computeDCTBlocks`** — pre-computes luma DCT coefficients before chroma encoding begins
- **`computeCfLCoefficient`** — per-block least-squares regression (`Σ(L·C) / Σ(L·L)`) over AC coefficients, DC excluded
- **`applyCfLPrediction`** / **`reconstructFromCfL`** — forward/inverse CfL transform on chroma DCT blocks
- **`encode()`** restructured to pass luma DCT grid to chroma channel encoding
- CfL coefficient written to bitstream per chroma block as fixed-point (`× cflScaleFactor`)

### Tests (14 new, 205 total)

- Coefficient computation: perfect/zero/negative/uncorrelated correlation, DC exclusion
- Prediction: residual energy reduction, DC preservation, round-trip reconstruction
- Integration: full RGB pipeline, single-channel graceful no-op

### Milestone update

- `MILESTONES.md`: marked CfL as complete in Milestone 3

body:
FlatBuffers 25.x removed the `--js` code generator. JavaScript bindings now require TypeScript generation followed by transpilation.

## Changes

- **Version references**: Updated `scripts/update_dependencies.sh` and `third_party/flatbuffers/` to v25.9.23

- **C++ headers**: Regenerated `generated/include/engine/api/flatbuffers/*.h` with flatc 25.9.23. Version assertions now check for 25.9.23.

- **JavaScript generation workflow** (new approach):
  ```bash
  # Generate TypeScript from schemas
  flatc --ts --ts-flat-files -o /tmp/output include/engine/api/flatbuffers/fbresult.fbs
  
  # Bundle to JavaScript with esbuild
  esbuild /tmp/output/osrm/engine/api/fbresult.ts --format=esm --bundle --external:flatbuffers
  ```
  
  The bundled output is wrapped to maintain the existing `osrm.engine.api.fbresult.*` namespace for backward compatibility with existing test code.

- **Result**: `features/support/fbresult_generated.js` reduced from 3,971 to 1,419 lines while preserving identical API surface.

## Summary
Adds navigation from PDF Remediation Plan page to the existing Comparison Dashboard, completing Phase 4 frontend integration.

## Changes
✅ **Added "View All Changes" button** to PDF Remediation Plan page
- Appears when remediation has been performed (remediatedFileUrl exists)
- Navigates to `/remediation/:jobId/comparison` route
- Uses ListTree icon for visual consistency
- Positioned before Download and Re-audit buttons

## How It Works

### Integration Points
1. **PDF Remediation Plan Page** → "View All Changes" button → **Comparison Dashboard**
2. **Comparison Dashboard** uses existing components:
   - ComparisonHeader (summary stats)
   - FilterBar (filter by type, severity, status, WCAG)
   - IssueNavigator (prev/next through changes)
   - CodeComparisonPanel (before/after diff view)

### Backend Integration
- Uses existing comparison API endpoints (already implemented in PR s4cindia/ninja-backend#185)
- `GET /api/jobs/:jobId/comparison` - Summary + changes list
- `GET /api/jobs/:jobId/comparison/filter` - Filtered results
- `GET /api/jobs/:jobId/comparison/changes/:changeId` - Individual change details

## What's Already Built

✅ **Types & API Service** - `src/types/comparison.ts`, `src/services/comparison.service.ts`
✅ **Comparison Page** - `src/pages/ComparisonPage.tsx` (already exists for EPUB)
✅ **Components** - FilterBar, IssueNavigator, CodeComparisonPanel, ComparisonHeader
✅ **Route** - `/remediation/:jobId/comparison` (already registered in App.tsx)

## What Works for PDF
- ✅ Summary statistics (total, applied, rejected, skipped, failed)
- ✅ Filtering by changeType, severity, status, wcagCriteria
- ✅ Pagination through changes
- ✅ Code view (before/after diff)
- ❌ Visual view (N/A for PDF - only works for EPUB)

**Note:** Visual comparison is EPUB-specific and will show as "N/A" for PDF files. The code view works perfectly for showing PDF metadata changes.

```
 installed nemo-git-integration package post-removal script subprocess was killed by signal (Hangup)
```

The `restart_nemo()` functions attempted GUI operations in headless environments, causing the script to receive SIGHUP and terminate.

## Changes

**debian/postrm**
- Detect non-interactive environments before attempting Nemo operations
- Check for running Nemo processes via `pgrep` before signaling
- Add 2-second timeout wrapper to prevent hangs

**uninstall.sh**
- Apply same environment detection logic for consistency
- Skip `nemo -q` and restart operations when headless

## Environment Detection

```bash
restart_nemo() {
    # Skip in CI/headless environments
    if [ -z "${DISPLAY:-}" ] || [ ! -t 0 ] || [ -n "${DEBIAN_FRONTEND:-}" ]; then
        log_info "Skipping Nemo restart (non-interactive environment)"
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Only signal if processes exist
    if ! pgrep -x nemo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        log_info "No Nemo processes running, skipping restart."
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Timeout wrapper prevents hangs
    timeout 2 pkill -HUP nemo 2>/dev/null || true
}
```

Package removal now succeeds in CI while maintaining proper Nemo restart behavior in desktop environments.

author: alaudaa-renovate[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | Age | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [github.com/go-git/go-git/v5](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git) | `v5.13.2` -> `v5.16.5` | [![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/go/github.com%2fgo-git%2fgo-git%2fv5/v5.16.5?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/go/github.com%2fgo-git%2fgo-git%2fv5/v5.13.2/v5.16.5?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-25934](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-37cx-329c-33x3)

### Impact 

A vulnerability was discovered in `go-git` whereby data integrity values for `.pack` and `.idx` files were not properly verified. This resulted in `go-git` potentially consuming corrupted files, which would likely result in unexpected errors such as `object not found`.

For context, clients fetch [`packfiles`](https://git-scm.com/docs/pack-protocol#_packfile_data) from upstream Git servers. Those files contain a checksum of their contents, so that clients can perform integrity checks before consuming it. The pack indexes (`.idx`) are [generated](https://git-scm.com/docs/pack-format) locally by `go-git`, or the `git` cli, when new `.pack` files are received and processed. The integrity checks for both files were not being verified correctly.

Note that the lack of verification of the packfile checksum has no impact on the trust relationship between the client and server, which is enforced based on the protocol being used (e.g. TLS in the case of `https://` or known hosts for `ssh://`). In other words, the packfile checksum verification does not provide any security benefits when connecting to a malicious or compromised Git server.

### Patches

Users should upgrade to `v5.16.5`, or the latest `v6` [pseudo-version](https://go.dev/ref/mod#pseudo-versions), in order to mitigate this vulnerability.

### Workarounds

In case updating to a fixed version of `go-git` is not possible, users can run [git fsck](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fsck) from the `git` cli to check for data corruption on a given repository. 

### Credit

Thanks @​N0zoM1z0 for finding and reporting this issue privately to the `go-git` project.

author: willseed
body:
## Problem

Material Icons render as raw ligature text (e.g. `info`, `edit_location_alt`, `send`) instead of icon glyphs on initial page load — especially on slow connections or first visits.

## Root Cause

Angular's **Beasties** (critical CSS inliner) defers the full stylesheet via `media="print"`. Since no `<mat-icon>` elements exist in the initial static HTML, the Material Icons `@font-face` and `.material-icons` class are not considered critical and are deferred, causing a **Flash of Unstyled Text (FOUT)**.

## Fix

- Add `@font-face` and `.material-icons` class directly in `index.html` as inline `<style>` so they are never deferred by Beasties
- Add `<link rel="preload">` for the font file for earliest possible fetch
- Copy the `.woff2` font to `public/` for a stable, hash-free URL
- Remove the now-redundant `src/material-icons.scss`

## Testing

- ✅ All 223 tests pass
- ✅ Production build succeeds
- ✅ Font file included in service worker cache
- ✅ No duplicate `@font-face` declarations

- return explicit stop outcome metadata (including timeout/force-kill) from todo-runner pause/delete IPC handlers and shared API types

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes process termination and IPC contract for pausing/deleting jobs; incorrect handling could leave jobs running, fail to delete, or surface new UI errors under timeout/kill edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes `todoRunner` pause/delete to *await* managed process termination instead of fire-and-forget SIGTERM + delayed force-kill.

> Main-process handlers now return structured results (`TodoRunnerStopOutcome`, `TodoRunnerDeleteResult`, `TodoRunnerPauseResult`) including whether the job was running, whether it stopped, and whether termination timed out or escalated to SIGKILL; delete additionally disables the job (without deleting) on stop timeout and cleans up more per-job state on success.

> Renderer settings actions and smoke tests are updated to consume these return values and surface timeout failures (throwing when pause/delete didn’t fully stop/delete).

author: scylladbbot
body:
When `test_autoretrain_dict` was originally written, the default
`sstable_compression_user_table_options` was `LZ4Compressor`. The
test assumed (correctly) that initially the compression doesn't use
a trained dictionary, and later in the test scenario, it changed
the algorithm to one with a dictionary.

However, the default `sstable_compression_user_table_options` is now
`LZ4WithDictsCompressor`, so the old assumption is no longer correct.
As a result, the assertion that data is initially not compressed well
may or may not fail depending on dictionary training timing.

To fix this, this commit explicitly sets `ZstdCompressor`
as the initial `sstable_compression_user_table_options`, ensuring that
the assumption that initial compression is without a dictionary
is always met.

Note: `ZstdCompressor` differs from the former default `LZ4Compressor`.
However, it's a better choice — the test aims to show the benefit of
using a dictionary, not the benefit of Zstd over LZ4 (and the test uses
ZstdWithDictsCompressor as the algorithm with the dictionary).

Fixes: https://github.com/scylladb/scylladb/issues/28204
Backport: 2025.4, as test already failed there (and also backport to 2026.1 to make everything consistent).

author: landonthemoonn
body:
## Summary
Restructured the application from a monolithic single-component design into a modular, context-driven architecture with dedicated page components for each journey stage. Introduced comprehensive mock data for San Francisco apartment listings and moving tasks.

## Key Changes

### Architecture & State Management
- **Created context providers** (`ListingsContext`, `JourneyContext`) to manage global state for listings, saved apartments, active stage, and filters
- **Extracted page components** for each stage: `Scout`, `Compare`, `Decide`, `Secure`, `Plan`, `Settle` (replacing inline views in App.tsx)
- **Refactored App.tsx** from 295 lines to 106 lines, now serving as a shell that routes between stages and provides context

### New Components
- **Navigation**: `CurvedPath` — signature S-curve stage navigation menu (desktop-only, hidden on mobile)
- **Scout stage**: `AIInput`, `FilterPills`, `ListingCard`, `FloatingCompare` — apartment discovery UI
- **Shared**: `StageHeader` — consistent page header across all stages
- **Comparison**: `Compare` page with side-by-side apartment analysis
- **Decision support**: `Decide` page with radar charts and priority weighting
- **Application tracking**: `Secure` page for document uploads and lease review
- **Task management**: `Plan` page with moving timeline and progress tracking
- **Settlement**: `Settle` page for post-move checklist

### Data & Types
- **Created comprehensive type definitions** (`types/index.ts`): `Listing`, `Stage`, `MovingTask`, `Application`, `SettleItem`, etc.
- **Added mock data** (`utils/mockData.ts`): 15 San Francisco apartment listings with AI insights, 20+ moving tasks, application templates, and settlement checklist items
- **Replaced hardcoded NYC data** with realistic SF neighborhoods (Mission District, Castro, SOMA, etc.)

### UI/UX Improvements
- **AI match indicators**: Perfect/Maybe/Dealbreaker badges with contextual insights
- **Progress visualization**: Circular progress rings, radar charts, and animated progress bars
- **Energy-aware task management**: Tasks tagged with energy levels (low/medium/high) for ADHD-friendly planning
- **Responsive design**: Mobile-first with hidden desktop navigation on small screens
- **Smooth animations**: Motion transitions on all stage changes and interactive elements

### Code Organization
- Separated concerns: pages handle layout/logic, components handle UI, contexts handle state
- Consistent naming conventions and file structure
- Reusable filter and comparison logic extracted to contexts

## Notable Implementation Details
- Filter system supports multi-select with "All Listings" reset behavior
- Saved apartments persist in context state across stage navigation
- Mock data includes realistic details: pet policies, laundry, transit access, available dates
- Radar chart in Decide stage dynamically calculates match scores based on user priorities
- Progress calculations use memoization to prevent unnecessary recalculations

body:
## Description

### Motivation

Some consumers of the API still rely on `deviceId`, while the data model has already moved to `deviceKey` as the primary identifier. Removing `deviceId` entirely would break backward compatibility for existing clients.

### Why this improves the project

This change reintroduces `DeviceId` on the `Media` model as an explicitly **deprecated** field. It allows legacy integrations to continue functioning while clearly signaling that `deviceKey` should be used going forward. This provides a safe migration path, reduces the risk of breaking changes, and keeps the model aligned with current and future usage without sacrificing compatibility.

author: avivbichachi
body:
## What
Extend the workout session summary endpoint to include per-muscle aggregation totals
(sets, reps, volume) based on each exercise’s `primaryMuscle`.

## Why
Muscle-level aggregation is a core building block for progress dashboards and trend
detection. It allows us to measure workload distribution and later classify progress
by muscle group over time windows.

## Scope
- Add `primaryMuscle` to the summary query selection
- Aggregate `muscleTotals` for a session (sets/reps/volume)
- Keep existing exercise-level summary intact

## Out of scope
- Muscle-level progress vs previous session
- Rolling window trends (4–6 weeks)
- UI changes (dashboard charts/tiles)

## Implementation details
- Aggregation computed in-memory while iterating performed sets
- `muscleTotals` returned as a sorted array for stable UI output
- No schema changes required (uses existing `Exercise.primaryMuscle`)

## How to test
1. Ensure exercises have `primaryMuscle` populated (seed or create via API)
2. Start a workout session and log sets for multiple exercises
3. Finish the session
4. Call `GET /api/workouts/sessions/:sessionId/summary`
5. Verify `muscleTotals` exists and totals match performed sets
   - totals.totalSets should equal sum of muscleTotals.totalSets

## Notes
- Next issue will add muscle-level comparison vs previous same-day session (Issue #50)

## Closes
Closes #48

author: copilot
body:
`preload.js` was the only file hardcoding 30+ IPC channel name strings instead of importing from `shared/constants.js`. A channel rename in `constants.js` would silently break the IPC bridge with no error.

- **`preload.js`**: Import all IPC/event channel constants from `shared/constants.js` instead of duplicating string literals

```js
// Before
getSettings: () => ipcRenderer.invoke('get-settings'),

// After
const { IPC_GET_SETTINGS, ... } = require('./shared/constants.js');
getSettings: () => ipcRenderer.invoke(IPC_GET_SETTINGS),
```

- **`constants.js`**: Add module-level JSDoc documenting the naming conventions (`IPC_*` = invoke/handle, `EVENT_*` = one-way events), how to add new channels (constants.js → ipc-handlers.js → preload.js), and which files consume this module. Added per-section comments explaining purpose and consumers.

author: dantop114
body:
## Summary

Closes #1037

When the write rate is low and values are small, the memtable may never reach `l0_sst_size_bytes`. This prevents WAL garbage collection and increases recovery time.

This PR adds a hard-coded WAL flush count threshold (`MAX_WAL_FLUSHES_BEFORE_L0_FLUSH = 4096`, discussed in the issue) that forces a memtable freeze (and subsequent L0 flush) when the number of WAL flushes since the last freeze reaches the limit regardless of the memtable size.

## Changes

- Modified `maybe_freeze_memtable` to track the WAL ID gap since the last memtable freeze, triggering a freeze when the gap reaches `MAX_WAL_FLUSHES_BEFORE_L0_FLUSH` or the estimated encoded size threshold is hit. 
- Added `test_put_flushes_memtable_after_max_entries` test that verifies a flush is triggered by flush count

author: scylladbbot
body:
Prevent launching hundreds or thousands of fibers during multipart uploads by capping concurrent part submissions to 16.

Fixes: https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/CUSTOMER-139

Must be ported back to 2025.3/4 and 2026.1 since it is supposed to fix the time skew problem we observe in production clusters

### Fix validation
It is quite complicated to test the fix without creating some test that will run 15+ minutes with real AWS S3

manually verivied with `perf_s3_client` executed as below
```
perf_s3_client --smp 1 --operation upload --sockets 2 --object_name random.bin
```
`--sockets 2` is the real life scenario, this is the amount of sockets we use in production code
the `random.bin` is 8GiB and is know to start emitting warnings about time skew without the fix after 15 minutes of uploading

With this fix applied the same `perf_s3_client` finishes the execution afterr 18 minutes without a single warning

We are talking about warnings and not errors since we have retry mechanism which will create a situation when we have to create a really huge file with the test running hours in order to fail

cc: @mitso23 

- (cherry picked from commit 034c6fbd87c6c1d8ba0c512c7669d8ef5d9d8726)

Implemented an incremental fetch strategy for the OHLC data in `dashboard.py`. Instead of fetching the entire table every 5 seconds, the dashboard now maintains a local cache in `st.session_state` and only queries for new rows based on the last timestamp. 

Key changes:

## Summary

This PR eliminates code duplication by refactoring six separate memory functions into two unified, parameterized functions while maintaining backward compatibility.

- `SaveMemory1()`, `SaveMemory2()`, `SaveMemory3()` - 3 nearly identical functions

- ✅ `SaveMemory(memoryNum int)` - Single unified function with parameter

Introduces `filter_committed_height` on `WalletInterface`, separate from `synced_height`. `process_block` updates `synced_height` per-block (needed for balance/maturity calculations), but `FiltersManager` uses `filter_committed_height` for restart recovery. It's not the best solution I think, hence I added the TODO for now. I will look into this at some point later.

author: isaac-levine
body:
Fixes the Cincinnati 336-unit deal stuck in a retry loop.

When a deal is partially processed and the SQS message retries, the pre-generated `dealId` already exists in the DB, causing a unique constraint violation on every retry. Switches `deal.create()` to `deal.upsert()` so retries are idempotent — if the deal already exists, it's a no-op and processing continues.

## Critical Bug: Integration Wrapper Calls Wrong Modal Function

The new `NominationIntroModal` module was successfully created and works correctly, but the integration wrapper in `js/ui.phase-intro-integration.js` is calling the **wrong function name**, causing the game to halt after the plea completes.

**Current flow (BROKEN):**
1. User dismisses nomination modal OR submits plea
2. `NominationIntroModal.show()` promise resolves ✅
3. Integration wrapper is awaiting `showNominationIntroModal()` (OLD function) ❌
4. Integration wrapper never receives the resolution ❌
5. `renderNomsPanel()` never gets called ❌
6. Game halts ❌

### Root Cause

In `js/ui.phase-intro-integration.js` line 161, the wrapper calls:

```javascript
if (shouldShowIntro && typeof global.showNominationIntroModal === 'function') {
  await global.showNominationIntroModal();  // ← WRONG! This is the OLD function
```

But the **new module** in `js/nomination-intro-modal.js` exposes:

```javascript
global.NominationIntroModal = {
  show: show  // ← The NEW function is NominationIntroModal.show()
};
```

### Evidence from User Testing

The user confirmed:
- `typeof window.NominationIntroModal?.show === 'function'` returns `true` ✅
- Modal shows correctly ✅
- Risk check works ✅
- Plea modal opens and closes ✅
- **BUT after plea submission, game halts** ❌
- Manually calling `window.renderNomsPanel()` unfreezes it ✅

This proves the integration wrapper is not receiving the modal's promise resolution.

### Solution

**File: `js/ui.phase-intro-integration.js`**

**Line 161 - Change from:**
```javascript
if (shouldShowIntro && typeof global.showNominationIntroModal === 'function') {
  // Mark as shown BEFORE showing modal to prevent re-entry
  g.__nominationsIntroShownThisPhase = true;
  
  try {
    console.info('[phase-intro-integration] Showing nomination intro modal');
    // Simply await the modal - no dual path, no custom event, no Promise.race
    await global.showNominationIntroModal();  // ← WRONG FUNCTION
    console.info('[phase-intro-integration] Nomination intro modal dismissed');
```

**To:**
```javascript
if (shouldShowIntro && typeof global.NominationIntroModal?.show === 'function') {
  // Mark as shown BEFORE showing modal to prevent re-entry
  g.__nominationsIntroShownThisPhase = true;
  
  try {
    console.info('[phase-intro-integration] Showing NEW nomination intro modal');
    // Simply await the modal - no dual path, no custom event, no Promise.race
    await global.NominationIntroModal.show();  // ← CORRECT FUNCTION
    console.info('[phase-intro-integration] NEW nomination intro modal dismissed');
```

### Additional Safety: Keep Fallback to Old Modal

To ensure backwards compatibility (in case someone hasn't deployed the new modal yet), add a fallback:

```javascript
// Check if we should show intro modal
const shouldShowIntro = !g.__nominationsIntroShownThisPhase;

if (shouldShowIntro) {
  // Mark as shown BEFORE showing modal to prevent re-entry
  g.__nominationsIntroShownThisPhase = true;
  
  try {
    // Try NEW modal first
    if (typeof global.NominationIntroModal?.show === 'function') {
      console.info('[phase-intro-integration] Showing NEW nomination intro modal');
      await global.NominationIntroModal.show();
      console.info('[phase-intro-integration] NEW nomination intro modal dismissed');
    }
    // Fallback to OLD modal if new one not available
    else if (typeof global.showNominationIntroModal === 'function') {
      console.info('[phase-intro-integration] Showing OLD nomination intro modal (fallback)');
      await global.showNominationIntroModal();
      console.info('[phase-intro-integration] OLD nomination intro modal dismissed');
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('[phase-intro-integration] Error showing nominations intro modal:', e);
  }
}
```

### Expected Behavior After Fix

**User flow:**
1. Nomination phase starts
2. New modal shows ✅
3. User clicks "Check risk" → risk shown ✅
4. User clicks "Make a deal" → plea modal opens ✅
5. User selects option and submits → plea processes ✅
6. Toast message shows ✅
7. Modal dismisses ✅
8. **Integration wrapper receives promise resolution** ✅
9. **`renderNomsPanel()` called immediately** ✅
10. Fullscreen nomination selector opens ✅
11. Game proceeds normally ✅

**No halt. No manual console intervention needed.**

### Files to Modify

- `js/ui.phase-intro-integration.js` — Update `wrapStartNominations()` function to call `global.NominationIntroModal.show()` instead of `global.showNominationIntroModal()`

### Testing Instructions

After deploying this fix:

1. Start a new game, become HOH
2. Nomination phase starts → new modal shows
3. **Test 1: Simple dismiss** — Click anywhere to dismiss → nomination panel should open immediately
4. **Test 2: Risk check** — Click "Check risk" → view risk → click "OK" → nomination panel should open
5. **Test 3: Plea flow** — Click "Check risk" → "Make a deal" → select option → submit → toast shows →...

</details>

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | Age | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [github.com/go-git/go-git/v5](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git) | `v5.13.2` -> `v5.16.5` | [![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/go/github.com%2fgo-git%2fgo-git%2fv5/v5.16.5?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/go/github.com%2fgo-git%2fgo-git%2fv5/v5.13.2/v5.16.5?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-25934](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-37cx-329c-33x3)

### Impact 

A vulnerability was discovered in `go-git` whereby data integrity values for `.pack` and `.idx` files were not properly verified. This resulted in `go-git` potentially consuming corrupted files, which would likely result in unexpected errors such as `object not found`.

For context, clients fetch [`packfiles`](https://git-scm.com/docs/pack-protocol#_packfile_data) from upstream Git servers. Those files contain a checksum of their contents, so that clients can perform integrity checks before consuming it. The pack indexes (`.idx`) are [generated](https://git-scm.com/docs/pack-format) locally by `go-git`, or the `git` cli, when new `.pack` files are received and processed. The integrity checks for both files were not being verified correctly.

Note that the lack of verification of the packfile checksum has no impact on the trust relationship between the client and server, which is enforced based on the protocol being used (e.g. TLS in the case of `https://` or known hosts for `ssh://`). In other words, the packfile checksum verification does not provide any security benefits when connecting to a malicious or compromised Git server.

### Patches

Users should upgrade to `v5.16.5`, or the latest `v6` [pseudo-version](https://go.dev/ref/mod#pseudo-versions), in order to mitigate this vulnerability.

### Workarounds

In case updating to a fixed version of `go-git` is not possible, users can run [git fsck](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fsck) from the `git` cli to check for data corruption on a given repository. 

### Credit

Thanks @​N0zoM1z0 for finding and reporting this issue privately to the `go-git` project.

body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL

💡 **Vulnerability:**
1.  **Excessive Data Exposure:** `PastStory.js` previously fetched the *entire* `snowball-fight` collection (potentially thousands of documents) and filtered them client-side. This exposed all users' story data to anyone inspecting network traffic.
2.  **Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR):** The component used the `uid` URL parameter to filter stories. This allowed users to potentially view others' stories by modifying the URL.

🎯 **Impact:**
-   **Data Leakage:** malicious users could scrape all stories.
-   **Privacy Violation:** users could see private stories of others.
-   **Performance:** fetching the whole collection is inefficient and unscalable.

🔧 **Fix:**
-   Created `src/firebase.js` to centralize Firebase initialization.
-   Refactored `src/PastStory.js` to use `useAuthState` from `react-firebase-hooks` for secure user identification.
-   Implemented a server-side Firestore `query` using `or` and `where` clauses to fetch *only* the documents where the authenticated user is an author.
-   Removed reliance on the insecure `uid` URL parameter for data fetching.

✅ **Verification:**
-   Verified syntax of `src/PastStory.js` and `src/firebase.js`.
-    Confirmed `react-firebase-hooks` is a valid dependency in `package.json`.
-   Ensured the query structure matches Firestore requirements for secure filtering.

author: mohamedelashri
body:
This PR introduces three independent features that together make ROOT-MCP easier to deploy, configure, and extend.

---

## 1. Optional native ROOT/PyROOT support

Adds optional native ROOT/PyROOT integration gated behind `enable_root: true` (config file, env var, or CLI flag). ROOT-MCP continues to work fully without ROOT installed.

**New MCP tools** (visible only when ROOT is available and enabled):

- `run_root_code` — execute arbitrary PyROOT code in a sandboxed subprocess with structured result capture (stdout, stderr, output files, execution time)
- `run_rdataframe` — compute RDataFrame histograms without boilerplate
- `run_root_macro` — execute C++ ROOT macros via `gROOT.ProcessLine`

**Key components:**

- Subprocess-based ROOT detection with version and feature probing (RDataFrame, RooFit, TMVA, Minuit2)
- AST-based code sandbox blocking dangerous imports, builtins, and attribute accesses
- Subprocess executor with timeout, output capture, and structured results
- 6 code templates for common ROOT operations (`RDataFrame`, `TCanvas`, `RooFit`, file writing, C++ macros)

---

## 2. Zero-config / permissive-default onboarding

Removes the YAML-editing barrier for new users. ROOT-MCP now works out of the box with no config file.

**New ways to start the server:**

```bash
# Inline data path — no config file needed
root-mcp --data-path /path/to/data

# Environment variable (colon-separated for multiple dirs)
ROOT_MCP_DATA_PATH=/path/to/data root-mcp

# Generate a starter config pre-filled with the current directory
root-mcp init --permissive
```


## 3. Full environment-variable and CLI-flag configuration

Every `config.yaml` field is now exposed as both a `ROOT_MCP_*` environment variable **and** a matching CLI flag. The merge order is:

```
defaults → config.yaml → ROOT_MCP_* env vars → CLI flags
```

CLI flags always win, making it possible to run ROOT-MCP in containers or MCP client JSON config blocks with no YAML file at all.

### Environment variables added (25 total)

| Section | Variable | Controls |
|---|---|---|
| Server | `ROOT_MCP_MODE` | `core` or `extended` |
| Server | `ROOT_MCP_SERVER_NAME` | MCP server name |
| Security | `ROOT_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS` | Colon-separated allowed path roots |
| Security | `ROOT_MCP_ALLOW_REMOTE` | `1`/`0` to enable XRootD/remote URIs |
| Security | `ROOT_MCP_ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS` | Comma-separated allowed URI schemes |
| Security | `ROOT_MCP_MAX_PATH_DEPTH` | Maximum directory depth |
| Output | `ROOT_MCP_EXPORT_PATH` | Export output directory |
| Output | `ROOT_MCP_EXPORT_FORMATS` | Comma-separated allowed formats |
| Output | `ROOT_MCP_ENABLE_EXPORT` | `1`/`0` to enable export |
| Limits | `ROOT_MCP_MAX_ROWS` | Max rows per call |
| Limits | `ROOT_MCP_MAX_EXPORT_ROWS` | Max rows per export |
| Cache | `ROOT_MCP_CACHE` | `0` to disable caching |
| Cache | `ROOT_MCP_CACHE_SIZE` | File cache size |
| Analysis | `ROOT_MCP_MAX_BINS_1D` / `ROOT_MCP_MAX_BINS_2D` | Histogram bin limits |
| Analysis | `ROOT_MCP_FITTING_ITERATIONS` | Fit iteration cap |
| Plotting | `ROOT_MCP_PLOT_DPI` / `ROOT_MCP_PLOT_FORMAT` / `ROOT_MCP_PLOT_WIDTH` / `ROOT_MCP_PLOT_HEIGHT` | Plot output settings |
| ROOT exec | `ROOT_MCP_ROOT_TIMEOUT` / `ROOT_MCP_ROOT_WORKDIR` | ROOT subprocess settings |
| ROOT exec | `ROOT_MCP_ROOT_MAX_OUTPUT` / `ROOT_MCP_ROOT_MAX_CODE` | Output and code size caps |
| Resources | `ROOT_MCP_RESOURCES` | Semicolon-separated `NAME=URI\|description` specs |
| Logging | `ROOT_MCP_LOG_LEVEL` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, or `ERROR` |

### CLI flags added (mirrors every env var)

All the above are also available as `root-mcp` flags. A few examples:

Container/Docker — no YAML file
```bash
docker run root-mcp \
  -e ROOT_MCP_MODE=extended \
  -e ROOT_MCP_ENABLE_ROOT=1 \
  -e ROOT_MCP_ROOT_TIMEOUT=120 \
  -e ROOT_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS=/data:/exports
```

Claude Desktop JSON config — no YAML file
```bash
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "root-mcp": {
      "command": "/path/to/venv/bin/root-mcp",
      "args": ["--mode", "extended", "--enable-root", "--root-timeout", "120"]
    }
  }
}
```

XRootD remote resource on the command line

```bash
root-mcp --resource cms=root://xrootd.cern.ch//store/data --allow-remote --mode extended
```

Restricted production deployment

```bash
root-mcp --allowed-root /data/physics --allowed-root /tmp/exports \
         --max-rows 100000 --cache-size 10 --log-level WARNING
```

⚡ Bolt: Optimized Gmsh mesh generation settings.

💡 What:
Updated `mesh_generation.py` to use the Delaunay algorithm (`Mesh.Algorithm = 5`) and enable multi-threading (`General.NumThreads = 0`).

🎯 Why:
The default Frontal-Delaunay algorithm (6) is slower for 2D meshes and does not parallelize effectively. Profiling showed that mesh generation took ~20s for 4000 points with default settings, while Delaunay with multi-threading took ~14-16s, a ~20-30% improvement.

📊 Impact:
Reduces mesh generation time by approximately 20-30% for dense airfoil meshes.

🔬 Measurement:
Verified by profiling `mesh_generation.py` with 4000 points.
Before: ~20s
After: ~14-16s
Note: Element count increases slightly (~13%) due to algorithm differences, but generation is faster. I/O time increases slightly due to more elements, but net generation time is improved.

Participation gate (`getModerationGateStatus`) only counted evidence moderations from `moderation_events`, causing company_request moderations to not count toward the required 2 moderations. Users who completed 2 company_request moderations were still auto-assigned items.

## Changes

**Count moderations from both tables**
- Evidence: `moderation_events` with action `approved|rejected`
- Company requests: `moderation_actions` with action `approve|reject`

```typescript
const { count: evidenceModerationCount } = await admin
  .from("moderation_events")
  .eq("moderator_id", userId)
  .in("action", ["approved", "rejected"]);

const { count: actionsModerationCount } = await admin
  .from("moderation_actions")
  .eq("moderator_id", userId)
  .in("action", ["approve", "reject"]);

const userModerations = (evidenceModerationCount ?? 0) + (actionsModerationCount ?? 0);
```

**Related fixes**
- Fixed company_request query: removed invalid `users ( email )` join, fetch separately
- Added `skipAutoAssign` param to prevent auto-assignment after moderation actions

body:
The `/join-tournament` command was rejected as invalid. The command parser regex `^/[a-z]+` matched only up to the first hyphen, extracting "join" instead of "join-tournament".

## Changes

- Updated regex pattern to `^/[a-z]+(-[a-z]+)*` to match hyphenated command names
- Moved regex compilation to package level to avoid repeated compilation overhead

```go
// Before: compiled on every command
regex := regexp.MustCompile("^/[a-z]+")

// After: compiled once at package init
var commandRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`^/[a-z]+(-[a-z]+)*`)
```

The pattern ensures hyphens only appear between letter sequences, preventing invalid commands like `/-` or `/command-`.

body:
## Summary
- Adds `BangBangPulseProblem` — a new problem template promoting bang-bang (piecewise-constant, few-switch) controls via exact L1 slack reformulation
- Supports `UnitaryTrajectory`, `KetTrajectory`, `DensityTrajectory`, and `MultiKetTrajectory`
- Uses 1 derivative level (vs 2 in `SmoothPulseProblem`) with `LinearRegularizer` on slack variables for exact L1 penalty on `du`

**Depends on**: harmoniqs/DirectTrajOpt.jl#50 (`LinearRegularizer` + `L1SlackConstraint`)

### Key differences from SmoothPulseProblem

| | SmoothPulseProblem | BangBangPulseProblem |
|---|---|---|
| Derivatives | `du`, `ddu` | `du` only |
| Regularization on `du` | L2 (`QuadraticRegularizer`) | L1 via slacks (`LinearRegularizer`) |
| Extra variables | — | `s_du ≥ 0` |
| Extra constraints | — | `L1SlackConstraint`: \|du\| ≤ s |

- [x] Solve test: Hadamard gate fidelity > 0.9 (achieved 1.0)
- [x] Slack verification: `s_du >= |du|` at all timesteps

## Summary

This PR includes performance optimizations, resource cleanup improvements, and type checking enhancements completed across multiple sessions.

## Key Changes

### Performance Optimizations (Commit: 3039787)
- **Issue B - Lightweight Freshness Check**: Split `_check_auto_reindex()` into two phases to avoid unnecessary HybridSearcher creation (~0.5-2s savings per search when index is fresh)
- **Issue C - Pool Config Caching**: Added caching to `ModelPoolManager._get_pool_config()` to eliminate log spam (10+ logs per search → once per server lifecycle)

### Resource Cleanup Pipeline (Commits: 3b95619, 3ca8b18, db77bff, 68ed1da)
- **Mandatory Pre-Reindex Release**: Added `_release_and_verify_resources()` to ensure clean VRAM state before full reindexing
- **Graph Storage Persistence**: Fixed graph_storage None errors during auto-reindex by preserving graph across cleanup
- **Model Key Preservation**: Fixed embedder reacquisition failures by preserving model_key through cleanup cycle
- **Routing Validation**: Added validation that restored model exists in active pool configuration

### Type Checking Migration (Commits: 3317ade, 26fcb65)
- **Pyrefly Integration**: Replaced mypy with pyrefly for faster, more accurate type checking
- **Type Error Fixes**: Resolved 28 pyrefly type errors across 8 files (improved type annotations, fixed imports)

## Verification

### Unit Tests
- ✅ All 891 unit tests passing (694 search + 197 mcp_server)
- ✅ Updated 13 query router tests for new config defaults
- ✅ Updated incremental_indexer tests for resource cleanup changes

### Production Validation
- ✅ Live search test: Confirmed lightweight freshness check and zero pool config spam
- ✅ Full reindex test: Verified clean VRAM transitions (0.00GB → 1.11GB → 0.01GB → 2.88GB)
- ✅ Resource cleanup pipeline working across both Qwen3-0.6B and BGE-code-v1 models

## Performance Impact

**When index is fresh (common case)**:
- Before: Two HybridSearcher instances created (one discarded)
- After: One HybridSearcher instance (for actual search only)
- Savings: ~0.5-2s per search

**Log cleanliness**:
- Before: "Using full model pool" logged 10+ times per search
- After: Logged once per server lifecycle
- Savings: 90% reduction in redundant INFO logs

## Files Modified (25 files, +530/-112 lines)

**Core Performance Fixes**:
- `mcp_server/model_pool_manager.py` - Added pool config caching
- `mcp_server/tools/search_handlers.py` - Split freshness check, fixed import path

**Resource Management**:

**Type Checking**:

- Multiple files - Fixed type annotations

**Infrastructure**:
- `start_mcp_server.cmd` - Added Windows launcher script
- `scripts/antigravity_bridge.py` - New MCP server bridge
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` - Added pyrefly hook

## Breaking Changes

None - all changes are backward compatible.

## Related Issues

Resolves performance bottlenecks identified in post-deployment monitoring:
- Double HybridSearcher creation on every search
- Excessive pool config logging
- Resource cleanup failures during full reindex
- Model key preservation across cleanup cycles

author: maxrink
body:
## Summary

Add **cosign keyless signing** and **SBOM attestation** to the release workflow. This enables consumers to verify the authenticity and provenance of container images published by this project.

## Changes

| Step | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Install cosign | Uses `sigstore/cosign-installer@v4.0.0` (SHA-pinned) |
| Sign container image | Keyless signing via Sigstore OIDC against the multi-arch manifest digest |
| Generate SBOM | Syft SPDX-JSON SBOM generated during the assemble job |
| Attest SBOM | Cosign attestation with `spdxjson` predicate type |

All signing steps run in the existing `assemble` job which already has `id-token: write` permission for provenance attestation.

## Verification

After a release, consumers can verify the image:

```bash
# Verify signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/telekom/k8s-breakglass@<digest> \
  --certificate-identity-regexp='https://github.com/telekom/k8s-breakglass/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer='https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign verify-attestation ghcr.io/telekom/k8s-breakglass@<digest> \
  --type spdxjson \
  --certificate-identity-regexp='https://github.com/telekom/k8s-breakglass/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer='https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
```

## Audit finding

Addresses **H5** (Supply-chain — missing cosign signing in release pipeline).

### Motivation
- Clicks on overview items (student, assignment, topic, standard) should open the group's work in a modal rather than rendering the group inline below the overview to match the desired UX.
- Reduce layout complexity and keep the overview as the primary canvas while surfacing group-level thumbnails in a focused, scrollable dialog.

### Description
- Added a `groupModal` dialog in `index.html` and removed the inline below-the-overview gallery so grouped work is shown in a modal gallery instead of inline rows.
- Updated `app.js` to route overview interactions to `openGroupModal(...)` and implemented `renderGroupModal()` to populate the modal with ordered group cards; cards inside the modal still open the existing focus modal and annotation tools via `openFocus()`.
- Preserved existing focus/annotation code paths (metadata, highlighter, stickers, clear) and wired modal open/close state to keep behavior consistent with sort and shuffle settings.
- Added modal styles and header metadata in `styles.css` and updated `README.md` wording to document the click-to-open modal gallery flow.

### Testing
- Launched a local server with `python3 -m http.server 4173` and verified it started successfully (HTTP 200 response from `curl -I`).
- Ran a Playwright script that simulated clicks on a student tile, an assignment timeline chip, and a topic centroid, and each click opened the group modal as expected (screenshots captured for each state); Playwright checks passed.
- Verified that work cards inside the group modal open the focus modal and that metadata/annotation UI remains functional (interactive checks via the test script succeeded).

author: shebeisen
body:
⚡ Bolt: Optimize WebSocket audio buffer handling

💡 What:
- Updated `ClientMessage` type in `shared/types.ts` to accept `Uint8Array` in `payload.data`.
- Modified `backend/src/ws-server.ts` `parseClientMessage` to pass the `Buffer` directly instead of extracting `ArrayBuffer` via `new Uint8Array(buffer).buffer` (which caused a copy).
- Modified `backend/src/ws-server.ts` `handleAudioMessage` to handle `Uint8Array` and `Buffer` inputs efficiently, using `Buffer.from(buffer.buffer, offset, length)` to create views instead of copies.

🎯 Why:
- The previous implementation copied every audio packet (20ms chunks) at least once, sometimes twice, increasing GC pressure and CPU usage.
- Audio streaming is a hot path; zero-copy handling significantly improves throughput and latency.

📊 Impact:
- Reduces memory allocations for incoming audio streams.
- Eliminates O(n) copy operation for every audio frame.

🔬 Measurement:
- Verified with `npm test` in `backend/` to ensure no regressions in logic.
- Compilation verified with `npm run build`.

---

body: ## **Description** Fixed the Token List Item V2 component to display prices for non-EVM tokens (e.g. Solana, Bitcoin). The V2 layout was only computing fiat prices using EVM market data, causing non-EVM tokens to show no price. This PR adds a lookup to MultichainAssetsRatesController for non-EVM assets so their fiat rate is used when available. body:
### Motivation
- Prevent flaky/false-negative market-closed checks by switching verify_e2e from parsing historical logs to reading a canonical structured executor metrics artifact.
- Ensure executor always emits a single-source-of-truth `data/execute_metrics.json` for run health and downstream checks, including early-exit (market closed) cases.

### Description
- Make `scripts/execute_trades.py` persist canonical executor metrics to `data/execute_metrics.json` on every run using an atomic write (`.tmp` → rename) and expose `METRICS_PATH` for tests.
- Extend the canonical metrics payload with normalized counters and fields: `skip_counts`/`skips`, `orders_submitted`, `orders_filled`, `trailing_attached`, `candidate_source`, `run_date`, and a structured `market_clock` (`ny_date`, `is_open`, `next_open`, `next_close`).
- Ensure market-closed early-exit writes `status="skipped"`, `skip_counts.MARKET_CLOSED == 1`, zero for order counters, and persists the metrics before returning success (rc=0).
- Replace the log-parsing market-closed checks in `scripts/verify_e2e.py` with metrics-driven validation that loads `data/execute_metrics.json` (or fails with a clear message if missing) and prints the relevant fields on failure.
- Add tests: `tests/test_verify_e2e_metrics.py` (new) verifies metrics-only market-closed PASS/FAIL modes and ensures `verify_e2e` does not read `execute_trades.log`, and strengthen `tests/test_execute_market_closed_skip.py` to assert the persisted JSON contents.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_verify_e2e_metrics.py tests/test_execute_market_closed_skip.py` and observed all tests passing (3 passed).
- Added/updated unit tests cover the new metrics-only market-closed checks and persisted artifact contents, and these tests were executed as part of verification and passed.

author: julianknutsen
body:
## Summary
- **Production fix**: When `os.ReadFile` fails transiently after claiming a nudge (e.g., Windows AV holding a share lock), unclaim the file (rename back to `.json`) instead of deleting it — prevents permanent nudge loss.
- **Test fix**: Add a straggler sweep after concurrent drains in `TestConcurrentDrainNoDoubleDeli`, mirroring real-world hook behavior where `Drain` is called repeatedly. This handles the case where all concurrent drainers fail `os.Rename` on a file due to a transient sharing violation.

## Root cause
On Windows, antivirus scanners and search indexers can hold sharing violations on `.json` files. When 5 concurrent `Drain` goroutines all fail `os.Rename` on the same file, the nudge stays as `.json` but no drainer returns it — appearing as a lost nudge.

CI failure: https://github.com/steveyegge/gastown/actions/runs/22066376229/job/63759176127
```
--- FAIL: TestConcurrentDrainNoDoubleDeli (0.08s)
    queue_test.go:545: concurrent Drains delivered 9 total nudges, want exactly 10
```

## Test plan

- [x] 50-iteration stress test passes
- [x] Race detector clean
- [ ] Windows CI passes (this PR)

body: ## Summary Two-service Docker application (Go API server + Python cron monitor) that detects users approaching their Windsurf credit cap, emails them a request form, routes approval through their manager, and updates the cap via the Windsurf API. ### Updates since last revision Addresses two outstanding review comments on `server/handlers/approval.go`: 1. **TOCTOU race fix**: All state-mutating UPDATE queries in `handleApproveAction` and `handleDenyAction` now include `AND status IN ('pending_manager', 'failed')` in the WHERE clause and check `RowsAffected()`. If another concurrent request already transitioned the status, the handler reloads the request and renders the current status instead of performing a duplicate write or Windsurf API call. 2. **GET /approve expiry check reorder**: `handleGetApprove` now loads the request and checks for terminal status *before* checking token expiry. Managers can view the outcome (completed/denied/expired) of requests they already acted on even after the approval token TTL has passed. This mirrors the existing pattern in `handleGetRequest` in `form.go`. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [x] **Verify `affected == 0` path is safe**: When `RowsAffected` returns 0, the code calls `h.loadRequest(req.ID)` and discards the error. Confirm this cannot nil-pointer or silently swallow a real DB error in `handleApproveAction` (lines ~247, ~285) and `handleDenyAction` (line ~326). - [x] **Confirm expiry reorder doesn't weaken security**: Expired approval tokens can now reach the `loadRequest` + JTI check + terminal-status render path. Verify this is acceptable and that no write operations are reachable with an expired token in `handleGetApprove`. - [x] **Build verification**: Go was not available in the dev environment, so the latest commit was not compile-checked. Run `cd server && go build ./...` to confirm. - [ ] **End-to-end test**: Spin up via `docker-compose up --build`, trigger a threshold notification, submit a request, approve it, and verify the cap is updated via the Windsurf API. Confirm emails render correctly (no stale `100%%` or `.0` issues from prior fixes). ### Notes - [Link to Devin run](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e2bc7d0a927b4fa99dce18572db3a0ce) - Requested by: @parkerduff ---

The [env] section in railway.toml sets NODE_ENV=production for ALL

devDependencies (typescript, @types/*). The previous fix tried to
override this with NODE_ENV=development in the buildCommand, but
Nixpacks runs its own install phase BEFORE the buildCommand where
NODE_ENV=production still applies.

Fix: Remove [env] section entirely so Nixpacks installs all deps
(including devDependencies needed for tsc), and set NODE_ENV=production
only in the deploy startCommand where it's actually needed.

author: lkishalmi
body:
Removed the now un-used `StoppableConvertor` from Lucene Support. I think that kind of convertor was introduced to be able to stop query processing with the use case when the sequential processing of Terms in Lucen 3.x would, the next element in the sequence would jump over to another field.

Since from Lucene 4 the Terms are grouped by fields, this functionality is no longer needed. Also it seems a bit weird to have a control logic built on an exception handling. 

The only instantiation of the `Stop` exception is the `QueryUtils.PackageFilter.STOP` which became unused with the Lucene upgrade.

💡 What: Replaced re.finditer with re.findall in evolutia/utils/math_extractor.py for extract_math_expressions and extract_variables.
🎯 Why: re.finditer creates match objects for every match, which adds significant overhead in Python when parsing large documents with many small matches (like variables). re.findall creates the list in C, which is much faster.
📊 Impact: Reduces execution time of extract_variables by ~34% and extract_math_expressions by ~21% in benchmarks.
🔬 Measurement: Verified with custom benchmarks and existing unit tests.

body:
### Motivation

- The feed UI was not updating when navigating pages because server fetches were not consistently keyed by `page`/`page_size` and Next.js server rendering/caching could return stale props.

### Description

- Read `page_size` from `searchParams` (falling back to `limit`) and normalize `page` and `pageSize` in `frontend/app/page.tsx` to compute `offset = (page - 1) * pageSize` and `limit = pageSize`.
- Include `page_size`, `limit`, `offset`, and `include_total` in the `requestParams` object passed to `getFeed` so server requests vary by page and page size (`frontend/app/page.tsx`).
- Update client-side pagination URL updates to set `page_size` alongside existing `limit`/`offset` so navigation and server parsing remain aligned (`frontend/components/feed/FeedList.tsx`).
- No change required to caching calls because the route already declares `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` and `getFeed`/`fetchJson` already use `cache: "no-store"` and `next: { revalidate: 0 }` (`frontend/lib/api.ts`).

### Testing

- Ran `npm run build` in `frontend/` and the build completed successfully.
- Launched the dev server and executed an automated Playwright script that navigated to `/?tape=all&page=2&page_size=25` and produced a screenshot confirming the request URL included `offset` and `page_size` (screenshot artifact produced).
- Dev-time fetch to the upstream API failed in this environment (`fetch failed`) due to upstream connectivity, so live-data verification against the remote API was limited, but request URLs and query keys were exercised and logged successfully.

author: gautxori-yuyu
body:
## Summary

This refactor moves filesystem pattern validation and opportunity object construction from the domain layer (`clsOpportunitiesMgr`) to the infrastructure layer (`FileSystemOpportunityProvider`), establishing a cleaner separation of concerns. The domain now receives fully-constructed domain objects instead of raw filesystem strings.

## Key Changes

- **FileSystemOpportunityProvider.cls**: 
  - Added `WithEvents mFSMonitoringCoord` to listen directly to filesystem events
  - Introduced two public events: `OpportunityDetected(op As clsOpportunity)` and `OpportunityRemoved(opportunityCode As String)`
  - Moved regex validation logic (`IsValidOpportunityName`) and opportunity construction (`BuildSingleOpportunity`) to private methods
  - Added event handlers for `OpportunityCreated`, `OpportunityDeleted`, and `OpportunityRenamed` that validate and emit domain objects
  - Made `Initialize` parameter `oFSMonitoringCoord` optional to maintain backward compatibility with existing tests

- **clsOpportunitiesMgr.cls**:
  - Removed `ProcesarCambiosEnOportunidades()` method (violated Single Responsibility Principle by applying filesystem regex)
  - Removed `ProcesarCambiosEnItemsOportunidad()` stub method (no valid callers)
  - Added `AddOpportunity(op As clsOpportunity)` with idempotent insertion by `Number` and ordered collection maintenance
  - Added `RemoveOpportunity(opportunityCode As String)` that cleans up current selection state if needed

- **clsEventsMediatorDomain.cls**:
  - Added `WithEvents mOpportunityProvider As FileSystemOpportunityProvider` field
  - Replaced five filesystem event handlers with two new handlers that receive domain objects:
    - `mOpportunityProvider_OpportunityDetected()` → calls `AddOpportunity()`
    - `mOpportunityProvider_OpportunityRemoved()` → calls `RemoveOpportunity()`
  - Maintained existing `mFSMonitoringCoord` subscriptions for non-opportunity events (template, gas, monitoring)

- **clsApplication.cls**:
  - Updated `mOpportunityProvider.Initialize()` call to pass `mFSMonitoringCoord` as third parameter
  - Updated `mEvMediatorDomain.Initialize()` call to pass `mOpportunityProvider` as sixth parameter

## Implementation Details

- **Idempotency**: `AddOpportunity()` checks by `Number` to prevent duplicates when FSWatcher fires after manual creation
- **Ordered insertion**: Maintains descending order by `Number` in the opportunities collection
- **Sealed path pattern**: `BuildSingleOpportunity()` seals the full filesystem path within the `clsOpportunity` object
- **Graceful degradation**: `ExtractOpportunityCode()` falls back to full folder name if no 9-digit prefix found
- **VBA limitation**: Uses concrete class type (`FileSystemOpportunityProvider`) with `WithEvents` since VBA doesn't support `WithEvents` on interfaces

## Architectural Benefit

The domain layer is now pure—it no longer knows about filesystem patterns, regex, or raw string validation. Infrastructure handles all filesystem concerns and delivers validated domain objects to the application layer, improving testability and maintainability.

### Motivation
- The scanner is slow when fetching candles for many symbols but must remain single-threaded to avoid Binance REST bans, so a faster sequential fetch path was needed.

### Description
- Added `_fetch_fast_ohlcv_rest(session, symbol, timeframe, limit)` which reuses a single `requests.Session` to fetch Binance Futures klines with retries, global rate-limiter waits, and backoff handling.
- Integrated a single `rest_session` into `scan_binance` when `fast_scan` is enabled and configured it with `HTTPAdapter`+`Retry`, ensuring the session is closed in a `finally` block.
- Updated per-symbol logic in `scan_symbol` to prefer the REST fast path and gracefully fall back to the original `fetch_ohlcv` path when REST is unavailable, while still using `GLOBAL_RATE_LIMITER` and ban-detection/backoff.
- Preserved the existing anti-ban behavior by keeping scanner execution effectively sequential (the `concurrency > 1` path remains forced to single-threaded) and avoiding parallel REST calls.

body:
### Motivation
- Some iOS/in-app browsers reject relative `fetch()` URLs with errors like “The string did not match the expected pattern”, causing UI requests to fail before reaching the backend.
- Ensure run and transpile actions reliably reach `/api/*` endpoints across strict browser environments.

### Description
- Added a shared `apiFetch(path, options)` helper in `index.html` that builds an absolute URL (using `window.location.origin` or a protocol/host fallback) and falls back to a conservative concatenation if `new URL()` fails.
- Replaced direct `fetch('/api/transpile/js')`, `fetch('/api/transpile/python')`, and `fetch('/api/run')` calls with `apiFetch(...)` so all run/transpile requests use the safe URL construction.
- Kept the existing behavior and error handling for transpile/run responses unchanged.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` which passed with no whitespace or patch issues.
- Ran the test suite with `python -m pytest -q`, which could not complete because the repository contains a local `types.py` that shadows the stdlib `types` module and prevents pytest from bootstrapping (fail).

## 🔒 Add Trivy Operator for Security Scanning

### What this PR does

Deploys **Trivy Operator** to the `observability` namespace for automated security scanning of container images, Kubernetes configurations, and compliance checks.

### Components Added

- **HelmRelease**: Trivy Operator v0.28.0 from Aqua Security
- **HelmRepository**: Aqua Security Helm repo
- **GrafanaDashboard**: Official Trivy Operator dashboard (ID: 16337)
- **Namespace**: observability (existing)

### Features Enabled

✅ **Vulnerability Scanning**
- Scans all container images in the cluster
- Reports CRITICAL, HIGH, and MEDIUM severity CVEs
- Ignores unfixed vulnerabilities to reduce noise

✅ **Kubernetes Configuration Audit**
- RBAC assessment
- Security best practices
- Infrastructure assessment
- Exposed secrets detection

✅ **Compliance Reports**
- Daily compliance scans (cron: 1 AM)
- CIS Benchmarks
- NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guide

✅ **Prometheus & Grafana Integration**
- ServiceMonitor enabled
- Metrics for vulnerabilities tracking
- **Grafana Dashboard** (grafana.com/16337) - Official Trivy Operator dashboard

### Configuration Highlights

```yaml
trivy:
  ignoreUnfixed: true
  severity: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM

scanJobsConcurrentLimit: 3
scanJobTimeout: 5m
scanJobTTL: 24h

operator:
  vulnerabilityScannerEnabled: true
  configAuditScannerEnabled: true
  rbacAssessmentScannerEnabled: true
  exposedSecretScannerEnabled: true

compliance:
  failEntriesLimit: 10
  cron: "0 1 * * *"
```

### Post-Deployment

After merge, Trivy will:
1. Scan all existing pods/images automatically
2. Generate VulnerabilityReport CRDs
3. Generate ConfigAuditReport CRDs
4. Expose metrics to Prometheus
5. **Dashboard available in Grafana** with vulnerability trends, top CVEs, compliance status

View reports with:
```bash
# Vulnerability reports
kubectl get vulnerabilityreports -A

# Config audit reports
kubectl get configauditreports -A

# Exposed secrets
kubectl get exposedsecretreports -A

# RBAC assessment
kubectl get rbacassessmentreports -A
```

### Grafana Dashboard

The dashboard provides:
- 📊 Vulnerability trends (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM)
- 🖼️ Top 10 most vulnerable images
- ⚙️ Configuration audit summary
- 🔐 RBAC assessment overview
- 📈 Historical trends

Access: **Grafana → Dashboards → Trivy Operator**

### Resource Usage

- **CPU request**: 100m (light)
- **Memory request**: 128Mi
- **Memory limit**: 512Mi

Scan jobs are limited to 3 concurrent runs to avoid cluster overload.

### Dependencies

- Depends on: `kube-prometheus-stack` (for ServiceMonitor)

---

**Ready to merge after CI checks pass.**

- ✅ Removed duplicate `compliance` key
- ✅ Removed Helm-specific `install`/`upgrade` keys (not needed in Flux HelmRelease)

author: kahtaf
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a new `agent-login/` research package focused on AI-agent authentication and product viability for an "Agent Login" integration flow.

The deliverables include a landscape report, investigation notes, a planning document, and a targeted viability/usefulness write-up for SMB SaaS teams with existing auth stacks.

## Problem

SaaS teams increasingly want coding agents to authenticate safely, but today the market is fragmented across OAuth delegation patterns, bot-verification controls, and secrets tooling. For teams already using providers like Clerk, BetterAuth, Google OAuth, or similar stacks, there is no clear, low-friction reference package for adding an "Agent Login" button without replacing existing identity.

Without this guidance, teams are likely to:
- ship brittle, one-off auth glue,
- overuse static credentials in agent runtimes,
- or avoid shipping agent-native features altogether due to security and implementation uncertainty.

## Root Cause

The current ecosystem has many partial building blocks, but lacks an integrated, developer-first narrative that combines:
- practical integration DX for existing auth systems,
- risk and abuse controls,
- and a viability framework for product decisions in SMB SaaS contexts.

## What Changed

Added five files under `agent-login/`:

- `agent-login/research-report.md`
  - long-form comprehensive landscape across identity, protocols, trust, and ecosystem signals.
- `agent-login/README.md`
  - concise synthesis of existing solutions, major gaps, and a recommended roadmap.
- `agent-login/notes.md`
  - research log, source validation notes, and key corrections.
- `agent-login/claude-plan.md`
  - planning/context artifact used to structure the investigation.
- `agent-login/validity-and-usefulness.md`
  - targeted viability and usefulness analysis for SMB SaaS teams integrating with existing auth stacks.

## User Impact

This improves decision quality for teams evaluating whether to build or buy an Agent Login layer by providing:
- a practical market read on what already exists,
- explicit integration paths that preserve existing auth,
- go/no-go criteria and a 90-day validation plan,
- and clearer risk framing for security/compliance review.

## Validation

Checks run for this PR:
- Confirmed staged scope was limited to `agent-login/*` before commit.
- Reviewed staged file list and diff stats.
- Verified branch push to GitHub succeeded.

Notes:
- This PR is documentation-only and does not modify runtime code paths.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent the orchestration phase from accidentally moving to `PLAN` when a `response.created` event is produced as part of an approval/confirmation prompt while a pending action exists.

### Description
- Modify `RealtimeAPI.handle_event` to detect confirmation-prompt response origins (`origin == "assistant_message"`) and, when a pending confirmation is active, skip the normal `OrchestrationPhase.PLAN` transition so the phase remains `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`.
- Add a dedicated log line: `response.created consumed by confirmation flow; phase remains AWAITING_CONFIRMATION` to clarify when an event was consumed by the confirmation flow without changing phase.
- Use `getattr(self, "_pending_action", None)` defensively to avoid AttributeError in test stubs that don't set the attribute.
- Extend tests: update `tests/test_realtime_response_origin_correlation.py` to record orchestration transitions and add `test_response_created_from_confirmation_prompt_keeps_awaiting_phase`; extend `tests/test_realtime_confirmation_flow.py` with a `_build_pending_action` helper and tests that verify accept/reject/timeout handling and the resulting orchestration transitions.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_realtime_response_origin_correlation.py tests/test_realtime_confirmation_flow.py` after installing `PyYAML` (needed for test import), and the full suite for those files passed with `15 passed`.

author: postmachines
body:
## Summary
Adds a new `ask-crypto` skill that integrates Velvet Unicorn’s `/ask` endpoint to provide AI-powered crypto intelligence within the agentic wallet ecosystem.

## What it does
Enables agents to:

- Answer natural-language crypto questions (e.g., “What do you think about Base?”)
- Analyze tokens and protocols (fundamentals, narrative, risk, momentum)
- Analyze EVM wallets (exposure, positioning, activity patterns)
- Provide market outlook and trade commentary
- Return optional proposed transaction data (`txdata`) for downstream execution skills

This skill is informational and read-only. It does not execute, sign, or broadcast transactions.

## What is Velvet Unicorn?
Velvet Unicorn is an AI-powered crypto intelligence engine developed by VelvetDAO. It processes natural-language crypto queries and returns structured responses including categorized analysis and optional transaction intent data.

Endpoint used:

`https://gentweet.velvetdao.xyz/ask`

Response structure:

- `meta_category`
- `vu_category`
- `answer`
- `txdata` (proposal only)

## How it works

The skill sends a POST request to the Velvet `/ask` endpoint with:

```json
{
  "question": "...",
  "context": "...",
  "userid": "0x...",
  "userid_sol": "",
  "previous_questions": []
}
````

The agent:

* Returns the `answer` directly to the user
* Treats `txdata` as proposed transaction data only
* Requires explicit user confirmation before passing any intent to execution skills (e.g., trade or send)

## Safety Model

* Read-only skill
* No signing or transaction broadcasting
* No automatic execution of `txdata`
* Explicit user confirmation required before any downstream execution

## Example Use Cases

* “What do you think about Base right now?”
* “Analyze this wallet: 0xabc…”
* “Should I rotate from UNI into ARB?”
* “Summarize risk and momentum for OP vs ARB”

author: bkrabach
body:
## Summary

Adds `.expanduser()` to three `Path()` construction sites in GlobTool and GrepTool where user-provided paths were not being expanded. Without this, paths like `~/.ai-os/workspace/` fail with "Path not found" because `~` is treated as a literal directory name.

This was the most user-visible bug — agents frequently pass `~/...` paths to glob and grep, causing silent failures and wasted retry cycles.

## Changes
- `glob.py:104`: `Path(base_path)` → `Path(base_path).expanduser()`
- `grep.py:305`: `Path(search_path)` → `Path(search_path).expanduser()` (ripgrep path)
- `grep.py:507`: `Path(search_path)` → `Path(search_path).expanduser()` (Python fallback)
- `tests/test_expanduser.py`: New test file (3 tests covering all paths)

## Overview

This PR implements a dual-contract system for tracking developer confidence oscillations and productivity metrics on the Stacks blockchain. The contracts gamify the psychological roller coaster between impostor syndrome and the Dunning-Kruger effect through measurable, transparent on-chain data.

## Motivation

Every developer experiences the constant swing between "I'm a genius" and "I'm a fraud." This implementation provides a humorous yet insightful way to track these patterns while demonstrating practical smart contract development.

## Implementation Details

### Contract 1: stack-overflow-dependency-coefficient (296 lines)

Tracks code authorship breakdown across four categories:
- Original work
- Stack Overflow contributions  
- AI assistance
- Prayers and luck

**Key Features:**
- Developer registration system
- Project-based authorship tracking
- Statistical aggregation and averages
- Dependency score calculation
- Reality check function with humor

**Public Functions:**
- `register-developer()` - Register a new developer
- `record-authorship()` - Log code authorship for a project
- `update-authorship()` - Modify existing records
- `deactivate-record()` - Mark records as inactive

**Read-Only Functions:**
- `get-authorship-record()` - Retrieve specific records
- `get-developer-stats()` - View developer statistics
- `calculate-dependency-score()` - Compute external dependency percentage
- `get-reality-check()` - Humorous assessment of code ownership claims

### Contract 2: tab-explosion-problem-avoidance-score (364 lines)

Monitors browser tab proliferation during development tasks with panic level correlation.

**Key Features:**
- Task lifecycle tracking (start to completion)
- Tab count snapshots with emotional states
- Panic level categorization (Zen Master → Existential Crisis)
- Difficulty rating based on tab growth
- User productivity assessment

**Public Functions:**
- `register-user()` - Register a new user
- `start-task()` - Initialize task tracking
- `record-tab-snapshot()` - Log tab counts during task
- `complete-task()` - Finalize task with metrics

**Read-Only Functions:**
- `get-task-record()` - Retrieve task details
- `get-panic-level()` - Calculate current panic indicator
- `get-average-tabs()` - View user averages
- `get-productivity-assessment()` - Comprehensive user analysis
- `get-global-stats()` - Platform-wide metrics

## Technical Specifications

**Language:** Clarity 2.0  
**Total Lines:** 660+ lines of contract code  
**Architecture:** Two independent contracts with no cross-contract calls  
**Data Structures:**
- 4 maps per contract for data persistence
- Data variables for global statistics
- Principal-based access control

**Security Features:**
- Input validation on all public functions
- Permission checks for unauthorized access
- Error handling with descriptive codes
- Safe arithmetic operations

## Testing

Contracts successfully pass `clarinet check` with only informational warnings about unchecked data usage (acceptable for this use case).

## Breaking Changes

None - this is the initial implementation.

## Dependencies

- Clarinet CLI (development)
- Stacks blockchain (deployment)
- No external contract dependencies

## Future Enhancements

- Web interface for visualization
- Integration with GitHub APIs for automated tracking
- Community leaderboards
- NFT achievements for productivity milestones
- Historical trend analysis

## Notes

The contracts include humor while maintaining functional integrity. The reality check and panic level assessments provide entertainment value alongside legitimate productivity tracking capabilities.

body:
MSVC generates C4244 warnings when compiling NotificationFCM.cpp due to implicit int64→uint conversions in jwt-cpp headers. AppVeyor builds were using stale headers from WindowsLibraries.7z because the jwt-cpp submodule wasn't initialized.

## Changes

- **Switch to jwt-cpp fork with MSVC fixes**: Update submodule from `Thalhammer/jwt-cpp@71c3d36` to `JurgenLB/jwt-cpp@f9f87d5` which includes explicit casts for `BN_num_bytes()`, `EVP_PKEY_size()`, `EVP_PKEY_bits()`, and `i2d_ECDSA_SIG()`

- **Fix include path ordering**: Prioritize `../extern/jwtcpp/include` before `../msbuild/Windows Libraries/include` in Release|Win32 configuration, add to Debug|Win32

- **Initialize submodule in CI**: Add `git submodule update --init extern/jwtcpp` to `appveyor.yml` before build step to ensure updated headers are present

Without submodule initialization, the build directory contains no jwt-cpp headers, causing MSVC to fall back to the outdated Windows Libraries version despite correct include path ordering.
